اقتدى (to take as pattern) occurs only twice, as a designed antithesis of emulation: 6:90 'fa-bihudāhumu qtadih' — the Prophet commanded to pattern himself on the guidance of the named prophets — against 43:23 the affluent deniers' boast 'innā ʿalā āthārihim muqtadūn,' patterning themselves on their fathers' footprints; right iqtidāʾ follows hudā, wrong iqtidāʾ follows āthār.

raʿd occurs only in these two passages, and each carries the full storm cluster (barq, ṣawāʿiq): in 2:19 thunder is the terror the hypocrites plug their ears against in fear of death, while in 13:13 the same thunder glorifies Allah's praise as He sends the ṣawāʿiq — one sky, read as dread by the faithless and as tasbīḥ by revelation.

The passive yuhraʿūn occurs exactly twice in the Quran: in 11:78 Lut's people rush headlong upon his house, driven by long-practiced evil, and in 37:70 the imitators are 'rushed along' on their fathers' footprints — the same rare passive both times depicting people propelled toward sin as if no longer steering themselves.

The rare epithet awwāh is applied only to Ibrahim, both times paired with ḥalīm and both times explaining his pleading for the doomed: 9:114 'inna Ibrāhīma la-awwāhun ḥalīm' on his istighfār for his father, 11:75 'la-ḥalīmun awwāhun munīb' on his arguing for the people of Lut — the same tenderness, bounded both times by final decree.

habāʾ occurs only twice, in matching accusative + passive-participle constructions of Day-of-Judgment pulverization: 56:6 the mountains are crumbled until they become habāʾan munbaththan (dust dispersed), and 25:23 the deniers' deeds are turned to habāʾan manthūran (dust scattered) — the Day's physics applied to a lifetime of works.

سرابيل occurs only in these two places: 16:81 'sarābīla taqīkumu al-ḥarra wa sarābīla taqīkum baʾsakum' — garments as Allah's protective favor — is inverted in 14:50 'sarābīluhum min qaṭirān' where the criminals' garments become tar that feeds the Fire: the very niʿmah of covering turned into punishment.

The exact three-word phrase 'مُقَرَّنِينَ فِي ٱلْأَصْفَادِ' (bound together in shackles) appears only in 14:49 — the criminals on Judgment Day — and 38:38 — the rebellious devils restrained under Sulaymān: the same formula of divine restraint applied to rebels human and jinn.

جزع appears only twice: 70:20 diagnoses man as 'idhā massahu al-sharru jazūʿan' — panic as his built-in response to evil — and 14:21 shows its terminal futility when the damned concede 'sawāʾun ʿalaynā a-jaziʿnā am ṣabarnā' — panic or patience now equal; both passages set jazaʿ against its opposite (ṣabr / the cure of 70:22) as the two responses to affliction.

The root's only two occurrences form one idiom: 4:46 'layyan bi-alsinatihim wa ṭaʿnan fī al-dīn' — tongue-twisting distorters stabbing at the religion — and 9:12 'wa ṭaʿanū fī dīnikum' — treaty-breakers stabbing at your religion; the same ṭaʿn-fī-al-dīn phrase marks verbal assault on the deen as the act that removes covenantal protection.

كُسَالَىٰ appears only twice, both times as the diagnostic epithet of the hypocrites' prayer: 4:142 'idhā qāmū ilā al-ṣalāti qāmū kusālā' and 9:54 'lā yaʾtūna al-ṣalāta illā wa hum kusālā' — the same rare plural fixing lazy, performative ṣalāh as the outward signature of nifāq.

The root ʿ-y-l occurs only twice and both times inside the same equation of poverty answered by divine enrichment: 93:8 'wa wajadaka ʿāʾilan fa-aghnā' — He found you poor and enriched you — becomes in 9:28 the community's promise, 'wa in khiftum ʿaylatan fa-sawfa yughnīkumu Allāhu min faḍlihi': the Prophet's biography generalized into the believers' economics.

سبأ: the Quran's only two mentions of the kingdom of Sabaʾ — 27:22 the hoopoe brings Sulayman 'certain news from Sabaʾ' at the kingdom's sun-worshipping zenith, and 34:15 names Sabaʾ's dwelling itself a sign ('two gardens, right and left') before narrating its fall — one kingdom traced from splendor to collapse across two surahs.

ثاقب: the identical rare epithet for a piercing celestial light — 86:3 defines the night-comer as ٱلنَّجْمُ ٱلثَّاقِبُ, the star that pierces, and 37:10 sends a شِهَابٌ ثَاقِبٌ, a piercing flame, after the eavesdropping devil — both times the adjective marks heaven's light as a penetrating power, not mere ornament.

دمع: the verbatim clause أَعْيُنُهُمْ تَفِيضُ مِنَ ٱلدَّمْعِ appears only twice in the Quran — 5:83 eyes overflowing with tears on recognizing revealed truth, 9:92 eyes overflowing with tears of grief at having nothing to spend for the expedition — the same overflowing-eyes formula marking sincere hearts in both scenes.

التقط: the Quran's only two uses of iltaqaṭa — 12:10 'some caravan will pick him up' (يَلْتَقِطْهُ) as Yusuf is cast into the well, 28:8 'the family of Pharaoh picked him up' (فَٱلْتَقَطَهُ) as Musa floats to the palace — the same verb of strangers lifting an abandoned child-prophet, each pickup becoming the hidden vehicle of divine providence.

بطر: the root's only two occurrences name the same disease of insolent exultation in blessing — 28:58 'how many a city We destroyed that بَطِرَتْ its livelihood', 8:47 'do not be like those who marched from their homes بَطَرًا and to be seen by people' (Quraysh to Badr) — the destroyed cities' diagnosis applied as a live warning to a marching army.

حلق: head-shaving as the pilgrimage rite — 2:196 legislates 'do not shave your heads (لَا تَحْلِقُوا۟ رُءُوسَكُمْ) until the offering reaches its place', and 48:27 shows the rite fulfilled in the true dream, 'you will enter the Sacred Mosque… مُحَلِّقِينَ رُءُوسَكُمْ' — the ruling and its narrative realization, both tied to the Hudaybiyah context of the obstructed pilgrim.

إصر: the crushing covenant-burden of previous nations — 2:286 the ummah prays 'lay not upon us an إِصْر as You laid on those before us,' and 7:157 answers it in the Messenger's job description: 'he lifts from them their إِصْر and the shackles that were upon them' — the du'a and its prophetic fulfillment built on the same rare noun.

نضد: divinely layered fruit — 50:10 palms with طَلْعٌ نَّضِيدٌ, spathes stacked in order as the proof-of-resurrection sign, and 56:29 the garden's طَلْحٍ مَّنضُودٍ, trees layered with fruit for the Companions of the Right — the same rare passive image of fruit arranged in tiers by a preparing Hand, once as evidence and once as reward.

عزّر: the rare verb of supporting/honoring the messenger, embedded in the same covenant formula in its only Quranic occurrences — 5:12 Banu Israil's covenant: 'believe in My messengers وَعَزَّرْتُمُوهُمْ (and support them)'; 7:157 the followers of the unlettered Prophet: 'those who believe in him وَعَزَّرُوهُ and support him and follow the light' — the obligation of the old covenant transposed onto the final Messenger.

نعاس (nu'as): the root's only two occurrences, both pairing drowsiness with amanah (security) as divine battlefield mercy — 3:154 'anzala 'alaykum... amanatan nu'asan' after Uhud's grief ↔ 8:11 'yughashshikumu al-nu'asa amanatan minhu' before Badr; the same two-word pairing, inverted, for the same sent-down calm.

شفا (shafa, brink): occurs only twice, both as an edge above the Fire — 3:103 'kuntum 'ala shafa hufratin min al-nar fa-anqadhakum' (the community rescued from the pit's lip) ↔ 9:109 'assasa bunyanahu 'ala shafa jurufin harin fa-nhara bihi fi nari jahannam' (the false mosque's founder collapses off the crumbling lip into the Fire) — same image, rescue versus fall.

استكان (to bend in yielding): appears exactly twice, both in the identical negated form — 23:76 'fama istakanu li-rabbihim' condemns hearts that would not bend to their Lord under punishment ↔ 3:146 'wa ma istakanu' praises the ribbiyyun who would not bend to their enemy after their prophet was struck; the same rare verb divides yielding into virtue or vice purely by its object.

خبال (khabal, ruinous corruption): its only two occurrences both name what insincere insiders work inside the believing community — 3:118 'la ya'lunakum khabalan' (outsiders taken as bitanah spare no effort in your ruin) ↔ 9:47 'ma zadukum illa khabalan' (had the hypocrites marched out they would only have added ruin); the same word, in the same accusative role, carrying the same warning about internal saboteurs.

مهيمن (muhaymin): the word occurs exactly twice — 59:23 as Allah's own name al-Muhaymin, the Watchful Guardian, and 5:48 the Quran sent down 'musaddiqan... wa muhayminan 'alayhi,' guardian over the Scripture before it; the Book is deliberately described with one of its Sender's names, entrusting it with divine guardianship over prior revelation.

قيلولة root (midday rest): its only two Quranic occurrences invert one image across judgment — 7:4 destruction falls on towns 'bayatan aw hum qa'ilun,' while they napped at noon in false security ↔ 25:24 the companions of the Garden are 'ahsanu maqilan,' granted the most beautiful noon-rest on that very Day; the ordinary siesta marks doom for one and perfected ease for the other.

أمل (amal, hope): the noun occurs exactly twice, staging false hope against true — 15:3 'yulhihimu al-amal,' hope as the distraction that lets deniers eat and drift until they know ↔ 18:46 the enduring righteous deeds are 'khayrun 'inda rabbika thawaban wa khayrun amalan,' better as an object of hope than the dunya's adornment; the Quran's entire use of the word is this contrast.

جرز (juruz, stripped-barren earth): its only two occurrences run the same cycle in opposite directions — 18:8 'We will surely make whatever is upon it sa'idan juruzan,' every adorned surface's appointed end ↔ 32:27 'We drive the water to al-ard al-juruz' and bring forth crops, barrenness as the canvas of resurrection; the rare word carries both halves of divine power over the earth's life and death.

بسر (to scowl/darken the face): the root's only two occurrences sit in consecutive surahs — 74:22 'thumma 'abasa wa basara,' al-Walid's chosen scowl as he engineered his rejection of the Quran ↔ 75:24 'wujuhun yawma'idhin basirah,' the scowling faces of the doomed awaiting the spine-breaking blow; the denier's contortion in dunya returns as the fixed expression of his face on the Day.

تبب: 111:1-2 'tabbat yadā Abī Lahab... mā aghnā ʿanhu māluhu' ↔ 11:101 'fa-mā aghnat ʿanhum ālihatuhum... wa mā zādūhum ghayra tatbīb' — both passages pair negated aghnā ('availed them nothing') with this rare ruin-root as the terminal verdict on what a denier relied upon (wealth / idols).

تبب: 111:1 Abu Lahab's hands and works 'perish' (tabbat... wa tabb) ↔ 40:37 Pharaoh's tower-scheme 'wa mā kaydu Firʿawn illā fī tabāb' — the same rare root twice seals a proud man's project against heaven as loss from its inception.

مُهْطِعِين: 14:43 the rare epithet for necks craned and gaze frozen toward the summons on the Day ↔ 70:36 the very same word for disbelievers craning toward the Prophet in dunya while denying him — the epithet stages the irony that the attention they perform now (70:36) becomes compelled forever then (14:43, 54:8).

هزم: 54:45 'sa-yuhzamu al-jamʿ' — the Meccan prophecy of the confident host routed (fulfilled at Badr) ↔ 2:251 'fa-hazamūhum bi-idhnillāh' — Talut's winnowed few routing Jalut's army after declaring 'how many a small band overcame a large one by Allah's leave'; the tradition ties that remnant (313) to Badr's count, making the Baqarah rout the paradigm the prophecy invokes.

سلخ (the flaying verb): 7:175 'fa-nsalakha minhā' — a man given Allah's āyāt slides out of them like a shed skin and Shayṭān overtakes him ↔ 36:37 'naslakhu minhu an-nahār fa-idhā hum muẓlimūn' — Allah strips the day from the night-sign and darkness is instant; the Quran's only two metaphorical uses of the butcher's verb, both times what is peeled away is illumination (signs / daylight) and what remains is darkness.

قردة: the identical sentence 'fa-qulnā lahum kūnū qiradatan khāsiʾīn' closes both 7:166 and 2:65 — the same Sabbath-breakers transformation, told in full (the sea-town, the fish, the three factions) in al-Aʿrāf and invoked in al-Baqarah as a punishment the audience 'already knew'.

قردة: 5:60 'jaʿala minhumu al-qiradata wal-khanāzīr' cites the same ape-transformation narrated in 7:163-166 as the historical precedent of divine curse when answering the People of the Book — the third and final occurrence of the word, all three pointing at one event.

تلقف: the verbatim clause 'fa-idhā hiya talqafu mā yaʾfikūn' appears in both 7:117 and 26:45 — the same moment of the same scene, Musa's staff swallowing the magicians' fabrications before Pharaoh's court, followed in both tellings by the magicians thrown down in prostration.

السلوى: 2:57 and 7:160 share the near-verbatim formula 'wa ẓallalnā ʿalaykumu/ʿalayhimu al-ghamāma wa anzalnā ʿalaykumu/ʿalayhimu al-manna wa-s-salwā — kulū min ṭayyibāti mā razaqnākum,' the same wilderness provision of Bani Israel (cloud-shade, manna, quail) told twice, both closing with 'they wronged only themselves.'

عبس: the only two persons in the Quran who ʿabasa — 80:1 'ʿabasa wa tawallā,' the Prophet's momentary frown at the blind seeker, recorded and corrected by heaven ↔ 74:22 'thumma ʿabasa wa basara,' al-Walīd's frown as he talks himself out of the revelation he privately recognized; two early-Meccan frowns at the moment of revelation set as mirror images, one instantly repaired, one hardening into 'this is only the speech of a man.'

رقي (ascent): 17:93 'aw tarqā fī as-samāʾ... wa lan nuʾmina li-ruqiyyika' — Quraysh demand the Prophet climb into the sky before they will believe ↔ 38:10 'fal-yartaqū fī al-asbāb' — Allah's taʿjīz counter-challenge to the same deniers: if they own the treasuries of mercy and the dominion, let THEM climb the ropes of heaven; the rare ascent-verb frames one polemic over who controls revelation from both directions.

شحن: the exact epithet ٱلْفُلْكِ ٱلْمَشْحُونِ 'the laden ship' — 26:119 Nuh and the believers saved in it after his plea, 36:41 the same laden ship made the standing sign that 'We carried their offspring'; Ya-Sin universalizes as āya the very vessel of Nuh's rescue.

شحن: ٱلْفُلْكِ ٱلْمَشْحُونِ verbatim again — in 36:41 the laden ship is the sign of God carrying humanity, in 37:140 it is the ship Yunus 'absconded to' (أَبَقَ); the identical rare epithet sets the ship of divine carrying against the ship of prophetic flight.

عجم: 16:103 refutes the slander that a human teacher taught the Prophet — 'the tongue of the one they hint at is أَعْجَمِىّ while this is clear Arabic' — and 41:44 runs the counterfactual 'had We made it a Quran أَعْجَمِيًّا they would have objected: a foreign book and an Arab?'; the same rare adjective carries the same polemic that the language objection was never sincere.

وجس: the rare Form IV أَوْجَسَ...خِيفَةً with an immediate لَا تَخَفْ — Ibrahim's concealed fear when the guests' hands do not reach the calf (11:70, 'they said: fear not') and Musa's inner fear before the sorcerers' ropes (20:67, 'We said: fear not'); the same verb-and-reassurance pair marks a prophet's hidden tremor answered at once.

زفر: the identical clause لَهُمْ فِيهَا زَفِيرٌ — 11:106 gives the wretched in the Fire 'violent exhaling and inhaling' (زفير وشهيق), 21:100 gives the worshippers of false gods the same زفير while their hearing is cut; the verbatim formula assigns Hell its one sound.

زفر: the زفير of the damned in 11:106 becomes the Fire's own breath in 25:12 — 'they hear from it fury and زفير when it sees them from afar'; the same rare roar-word is deliberately transferred from the punished to the punisher.

لذذ: the root of pure pleasure occurs only three times in the Quran, all in Paradise — the white cup لَذَّةٍ لِّلشَّٰرِبِينَ with no hidden harm (37:46) and the golden vessels holding 'whatever souls desire and eyes تَلَذُّ' (43:71); the same rare delight-word is reserved exclusively for the reward of the righteous.

خفت: the Form VI يَتَخَٰفَتُونَ occurs only twice in the Quran, both times as the hush of wrongdoers inside a shared delusion — the garden owners setting out 'whispering: let no miskīn enter upon you today' before their unseen ruin (68:23), and the criminals at the gathering 'whispering among themselves: you stayed only ten' after theirs (20:103).

نسف: Ta-Ha uses the same verb with the same cognate accusative twice — Musa's لَنَنسِفَنَّهُۥ فِى ٱلْيَمِّ نَسْفًا scattering the golden calf into the sea (20:97) and يَنسِفُهَا رَبِّى نَسْفًا pulverizing the mountains (20:105); the destroyed false anchor prefigures the Day when even the truest-seeming anchors are scattered.

رغد: Adam is commanded كُلَا مِنْهَا رَغَدًا in the Garden (2:35) and Bani Israil فَكُلُوا۟ مِنْهَا...رَغَدًا in the town (2:58) — the corpus file itself flags the echo ('Paradise echoes in the earthly command'); in both, raghad-provision is the prelude to a simple command disobeyed and the ease forfeited.

رغد: the secure town whose rizq came رَغَدًا from every place until it denied the favors and was clothed in hunger and fear (16:112) generalizes as a parable exactly the Adam pattern of 2:35 — abundant ease granted, ingratitude or disobedience, and the ease stripped away.

سأم: Fussilat negates the same rare verb twice as a deliberate contrast — those near your Lord glorify night and day وَهُمْ لَا يَسْـَٔمُونَ (41:38), while لَا يَسْـَٔمُ ٱلْإِنسَٰنُ مِن دُعَآءِ ٱلْخَيْرِ, man never tires of asking for his own good yet despairs at harm (41:49); two untirings, one of worship and one of appetite.

نقر: naqīr (the speck on a date-stone) occurs exactly twice, both in an-Nisa and both negated in the same accusative slot — if they held dominion لَّا يُؤْتُونَ ٱلنَّاسَ نَقِيرًا, they would not give people a speck (4:53), while the believers entering Paradise وَلَا يُظْلَمُونَ نَقِيرًا are not wronged a speck (4:124); human stinginess at its smallest unit set against divine justice at the same unit.

لفت: 11:81 and 15:65 give the angels' order to Lut in the identical wording وَلَا يَلْتَفِتْ مِنكُمْ أَحَدٌ ('let none of you look back') within the same night-escape scene — the same command in two tellings of one event.

سوغ: 16:66's milk is سَآئِغًا لِّلشَّـٰرِبِينَ ('easy to swallow for the drinkers') while 14:17's damned man يَتَجَرَّعُهُ وَلَا يَكَادُ يُسِيغُهُ can hardly make the festering drink go down — the root's only Quranic uses set swallow-ability up as a blessing granted in the dunya signs and revoked in the punishment.

حرّض: 8:65 يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِىُّ حَرِّضِ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَى ٱلْقِتَالِ and 4:84 وَحَرِّضِ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ are the only two occurrences of this imperative — the same directive to the Prophet to rouse the believers for battle, stated in two Madinan surahs.

طفأ: 9:32 'they want to extinguish (يُطْفِـُٔوا۟) Allah's light with their mouths — but Allah refuses except to perfect His light' is answered by 5:64 'every time they kindle a fire for war, Allah extinguishes it (أَطْفَأَهَا ٱللَّهُ)' — the root's only Quranic uses, in the same Madinan polemic, invert the agency: their extinguishing fails, His succeeds.

مرح: 17:37 and 31:18 give the identical command وَلَا تَمْشِ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مَرَحًا ('do not walk the earth in swaggering exultation') — once in the Isra ethical decrees, once in Luqman's counsel to his son — the Quran's only two occurrences of the prohibition.

أذقان: the word's only Quranic uses — in 17:107/109 the people of knowledge يَخِرُّونَ لِلْأَذْقَانِ, falling on their chins in prostration and weeping, while in 36:8 iron collars reach إِلَى ٱلْأَذْقَانِ forcing the deniers' heads up (muqmaḥūn) so the chin can never reach the ground — the same rare body-word staging prostration and its locked-out opposite.

جأر: 16:53 'when distress touches you, to Him you cry out (تَجْـَٔرُونَ)' — the instinctive bellow offered as proof of tawhid — meets its terminus in 23:64-65 where the luxury-softened bellow (يَجْـَٔرُونَ) under punishment and are told لَا تَجْـَٔرُوا۟ ٱلْيَوْمَ: the root's only Quranic occurrences, the same desperate cry heard in the dunya and refused when it comes too late.

صدف (ṣadafa, to turn away — the verb occurs only in al-Anʿām): 6:46 'look how We diversify the signs, then still yaṣdifūn' ↔ 6:157 triples the verb — 'who is more unjust than one who denies Allah's signs wa-ṣadafa ʿanhā; We will recompense alladhīna yaṣdifūna... bimā kānū yaṣdifūn' — the surah opens its indictment with the rare verb and closes it by hammering the same verb three times, framing turning-away-from-the-signs as al-Anʿām's charge.

بهيمة الأنعام: the construct phrase bahīmat al-anʿām occurs exactly three times in the Quran — 5:1 'uḥillat lakum bahīmatu l-anʿām' (made lawful under covenant) and 22:28 'yadhkurū sma llāhi... ʿalā mā razaqahum min bahīmati l-anʿām' (consecrated with Allah's name at Hajj) — the same unique formula binding lawful livestock to divine permission and divine mention.

بهيمة الأنعام: 22:28 and 22:34 repeat the near-identical clause 'wa-yadhkurū/li-yadhkurū sma llāhi ʿalā mā razaqahum min bahīmati l-anʿām' — first for the pilgrims at the House, then universalized ('for every ummah We appointed a rite'), the surah deliberately re-sounding its own sacrificial formula.

رهط (kin-band; only Quranic occurrences): 11:91-92 Madyan admits only Shuʿayb's rahṭ restrains their stoning and he answers 'a-rahṭī aʿazzu ʿalaykum mina llāh?' ↔ 27:48 'tisʿatu rahṭ' swear a kin-oath to assassinate Salih's family by night and plan to deceive his walī — in both punished-nation narratives the same rare clan-word names tribal solidarity as the real power a society weighs above Allah (and 11:95 itself pairs Madyan with Thamud).

أوثان + fabricated speech, twice paired: 29:17 'innamā taʿbudūna min dūni llāhi awthānan wa-takhluqūna ifkā' (you worship idols and manufacture a lie) ↔ 22:30 'fa-jtanibū l-rijsa mina l-awthāni wa-jtanibū qawla l-zūr' (shun the filth of idols and shun false speech) — the same rare word for idols deliberately yoked to fabricated falsehood in both commands, theologizing idolatry as a lie you make.

أوثان in Ibrahim's two diagnoses in al-ʿAnkabūt: 29:17 the idols are a manufactured lie that owns no rizq ↔ 29:25 'ittakhadhtum... awthānan mawaddata baynikum' — the same fabricated objects re-diagnosed as mere social glue that turns to mutual cursing on Qiyamah; two stages of one dismantling.

حسد of Ahl al-Kitab, twin diagnosis: 4:54 'am yaḥsudūna l-nāsa ʿalā mā ātāhumu llāhu min faḍlih' ↔ 2:109 they wish to turn believers back to kufr 'ḥasadan min ʿindi anfusihim min baʿdi mā tabayyana lahumu l-ḥaqq' — both passages name self-generated envy of Allah's freely allotted favor as the real engine behind theological objection.

حسد over divine allotment: 4:54 diagnoses envy of 'what Allah gave of His faḍl' (answered by the Book, wisdom, and mulk given to Āl Ibrāhīm) ↔ 48:15 the stay-behinds, barred by Allah's prior decree from Khaybar's spoils, project the same word back — 'bal taḥsudūnanā' — mistaking a divine apportionment for human envy; the rare root carries the theology of resenting what Allah distributes.

دحض, the argument that slips: 18:56 'yujādilu lladhīna kafarū bi-l-bāṭili li-yudḥiḍū bihi l-ḥaqq' — disbelievers argue with falsehood to make truth slip — ↔ 42:16 the verdict on the same enterprise: 'ḥujjatuhum dāḥiḍatun ʿinda rabbihim,' their argument itself is the thing that slips and collapses; the rare root states the attempt in al-Kahf and its reversal in ash-Shūrā.

هنيئا: the formula kulū... hanīʾan occurs four times in the Quran — three address the people of Jannah ('kulū wa-shrabū hanīʾan,' 52:19, 69:24, 77:43) and once, in 4:4, it blesses a husband consuming dower his wife has gifted 'ṭibna lakum ʿan shayʾin minhu nafsan... fa-kulūhu hanīʾan marīʾan' — the paradise formula of aftermath-free enjoyment granted in dunyā only where the giving is fully voluntary and rightful.

بديع السماوات والأرض: the epithet Badīʿu l-samāwāti wa-l-arḍ occurs only in 2:117 and 6:101, and both times it is deployed as the refutation of attributing a walad to Allah — 2:116 'ittakhadha llāhu waladan... badīʿu l-samāwāti wa-l-arḍ' and 6:101 'badīʿu l-samāwāti wa-l-arḍ annā yakūnu lahu waladun wa-lam takun lahu ṣāḥibah' — the One who originates without precedent or process needs no offspring.

قفّينا: the rare Form II qaffaynā ('We sent in succession') is a fixed prophetic-succession formula that always culminates in ʿĪsā — 2:87 'wa-qaffaynā min baʿdihi bi-l-rusul wa-ātaynā ʿĪsā bna Maryama l-bayyināt' ↔ 57:27 'thumma qaffaynā ʿalā āthārihim bi-rusulinā wa-qaffaynā bi-ʿĪsā bni Maryam' — the same verb, the same chain, the same terminus, each time setting up how the receiving community failed the gift.

صرخ, the scream no creature answers: 14:22 Shaytan on Qiyamah — 'mā ana bi-muṣrikhikum wa-mā antum bi-muṣrikhiyya,' I cannot answer your scream nor you mine ↔ 35:37 'wa-hum yaṣṭarikhūna fīhā rabbanā akhrijnā,' the damned scream in the Fire and receive only the rebuke that their time was already given — the same rare root marks the cry for rescue whose every created addressee fails.

صرخ: 14:22's mutual non-rescue ('not I your muṣrikh, nor you mine') ↔ 36:43 'fa-lā ṣarīkha lahum wa-lā hum yunqadhūn' — if He willed to drown them, there is no ṣarīkh, no answerer-of-the-scream, and no rescue 'except a mercy from Us'; both passages use the rare root to strip every rescuer but Allah.

شنآن (rancorous hatred) occurs only in the verbatim twin command وَلَا يَجْرِمَنَّكُمْ شَنَـَٔانُ قَوْمٍ — 5:2 'do not let hatred of a people who barred you from al-Masjid al-Haram push you to transgress' and 5:8 'do not let hatred of a people push you away from justice; be just, it is nearer to taqwa' — the same ruling stated twice in al-Maidah, first for the specific grievance, then generalized into the ethic of justice under hatred.

6:99 and 6:141 repeat the near-verbatim catalog وَٱلزَّيْتُونَ وَٱلرُّمَّانَ مُ(ت)شَٰبِهًا وَغَيْرَ مُتَشَٰبِهٍ plus ثَمَرِهِ إِذَآ أَثْمَرَ — the first commands 'look at its fruit when it bears' (the garden as sign), the second 'eat of its fruit when it bears and give its due on harvest day' (the same garden as obligation): one catalog, echoed for seeing then for owing.

مَلْجَأ (refuge) is the pivot of both: 9:118 the three left behind learn لَّا مَلْجَأَ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ إِلَّآ إِلَيْهِ — no refuge from Allah except back toward Him — and 42:47 warns of the Day when مَا لَكُم مِّن مَّلْجَإٍ يَوْمَئِذٍ — the dunya lesson and its final-Day confirmation stated with the same rare noun.

Within at-Tawbah the same rare noun draws the contrast: the hypocrites لَوْ يَجِدُونَ مَلْجَـًٔا أَوْ مَغَٰرَٰتٍ would bolt to any refuge away from Allah (9:57), while the three truthful discover لا ملجأ من الله إلا إليه — refuge exists only by returning to Him (9:118): false flight versus true return carried by one word.

The root's only active/passive pair: 25:29 وَكَانَ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ لِلْإِنسَٰنِ خَذُولًا — Shaytan the habitual deserter (intensive faʿūl) — and 17:22 the one who sets up another god فَتَقْعُدَ مَذْمُومًا مَّخْذُولًا sits abandoned (passive participle); both verse-final, naming the abandoner and the abandoned of the same misplaced reliance.

The same rare root completes the doctrine from the other side: 3:160 وَإِن يَخْذُلْكُمْ فَمَن ذَا ٱلَّذِى يَنصُرُكُم — only Allah's desertion leaves no helper, so trust Him — while 25:29 declares Shaytan خَذُولًا, the ally who always deserts; the root's three uses map who abandons and whose abandonment is fatal.

Both pair weakness with gray hair in the same breath: 30:54 states the decreed arc — مِنۢ بَعْدِ قُوَّةٍ ضَعْفًا وَشَيْبَةً, after strength weakness-and-gray — and 19:4 is Zakariyya presenting exactly that arc as his petition's credential: وَهَنَ ٱلْعَظْمُ مِنِّى وَٱشْتَعَلَ ٱلرَّأْسُ شَيْبًا, the ḍaʿf/wahn + shayb collocation lived from inside.

73:17's terror image is built on 30:54's decreed order: Allah appoints gray hair after strength at the end of life (ضَعْفًا وَشَيْبَةً), and the Day is measured precisely by its violation of that arc — يَوْمًا يَجْعَلُ ٱلْوِلْدَٰنَ شِيبًا, a Day that grays the children who should be furthest from shayb.

طبق carries only two Quranic uses: the layered heavens — سَبْعَ سَمَٰوَٰتٍ طِبَاقًا (67:3, verbatim in 71:15) — and 84:19 لَتَرْكَبُنَّ طَبَقًا عَن طَبَقٍ, where an oath-chain of sky phenomena (twilight, gathering night, full moon) culminates in riding 'layer upon layer'; classical exegesis (Ibn Abbas's gloss in the tafsir tradition, and the qira'ah addressed to the Prophet read as heaven upon heaven) ties the staged ascent directly to the layered-heavens image.

The participle مَّنثُورًا occurs exactly twice, both verse-final simile-closers in recompense scenes: the deniers' life-work becomes هَبَآءً مَّنثُورًا, scattered dust-motes (25:23), while the abrar are served by youths like لُؤْلُؤًا مَّنثُورًا, scattered pearls (76:19) — the same rare word marking the two ends of the scale, scatter as worthlessness versus scatter as abundance.

The same punishment scene with the same instrument-pair: 69:30-32 خُذُوهُ فَغُلُّوهُ ثُمَّ ٱلْجَحِيمَ صَلُّوهُ ثُمَّ فِى سِلْسِلَةٍ ذَرْعُهَا سَبْعُونَ ذِرَاعًا — shackle, Blaze, chain — and 40:71 إِذِ ٱلْأَغْلَٰلُ فِىٓ أَعْنَٰقِهِمْ وَٱلسَّلَٰسِلُ يُسْحَبُونَ — collars and chains dragging the denier into the Fire; salasil + aghlal + fire as one recurring tableau.

The same rare epithet of visible bliss on believers' faces on the Day: 75:22 وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ نَّاضِرَةٌ (faces radiant, gazing at their Lord) and 83:24 تَعْرِفُ فِى وُجُوهِهِمْ نَضْرَةَ ٱلنَّعِيمِ (you recognize in their faces the radiance of bliss) — naḍrah as the face-borne mark of reward in both scenes.

The only two Quranic pairings of نكس with رؤوس: 21:65 ثُمَّ نُكِسُوا۟ عَلَىٰ رُءُوسِهِمْ — Ibrahim's people flipped upside-down on their heads, relapsing right after admitting the truth — and 32:12 ٱلْمُجْرِمُونَ نَاكِسُوا۟ رُءُوسِهِمْ — the criminals heads-inverted before their Lord, confessing أَبْصَرْنَا وَسَمِعْنَا too late; head-inversion as the posture of truth refused in dunya and finally faced in akhirah.

Near-verbatim twin ruling: both list إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَٱلَّذِينَ هَادُوا۟ ... وَٱلصَّٰبِـِٔينَ/وَٱلصَّٰبِـُٔونَ وَٱلنَّصَٰرَىٰ then state the identical condition and promise — مَنْ ءَامَنَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلْيَوْمِ ٱلْءَاخِرِ وَعَمِلَ صَٰلِحًا فَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ — the same legislation that labels save no one without faith and works, stated twice.

The same Form III verb with the same subject and the same reversal: 2:9 يُخَٰدِعُونَ ٱللَّهَ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَمَا يَخْدَعُونَ إِلَّآ أَنفُسَهُمْ and 4:142 إِنَّ ٱلْمُنَٰفِقِينَ يُخَٰدِعُونَ ٱللَّهَ وَهُوَ خَٰدِعُهُمْ — the two-verse doctrine that the hypocrites' attempted deception of Allah rebounds, once onto themselves, once as Allah out-deceiving them.

هيأ: 18:10 the youths pray 'wa-hayyi' lanā min amrinā rashadā' and 18:16 answers with the Quran's only other use of this verb in the identical frame — 'yuhayyi' lakum min amrikum mirfaqā': du'a and divine answer built on the same morphology (hayyi'/yuhayyi' + min amr + accusative gift).

زلل: 2:36 'fa-azallahumā sh-shayṭānu' (Satan made Adam and his wife slip) ↔ 2:209 'fa-in zalaltum min ba'di mā jā'atkumu l-bayyināt' coming immediately after 'do not follow the steps of Shaytan' (2:208) — the surah re-runs Adam's Satan-caused slip as the warning template for the believers.

زلل: 2:36 Satan 'azallahumā' and Adam is then pardoned ↔ 3:155 'innamā istazallahumu sh-shayṭānu bi-ba'ḍi mā kasabū wa-laqad 'afā llāhu 'anhum' — Satan as agent of the slip followed by explicit divine pardon, the same arc from Adam to the Uhud deserters.

زلل: 2:36 Adam slips out of an already-granted station ↔ 16:94 'fa-tazilla qadamun ba'da thubūtihā' — the foot slipping after firmness; the rare root consistently frames sin as loss of secured footing, here applied to breaking a sworn covenant.

مجيد occurs only 4x in the Quran: outside the two 'glorious Qur'an' verses (50:1, 85:21, already linked), 11:73 'innahu ḥamīdun majīd' sealing the blessing on Ibrahim's house and 85:15 'dhū l-'arsh al-majīd' sealing Buruj's litany of divine names are its only uses — one restricted register of glory reserved for Allah, His Throne, and His Book.

كلب: the Quran's only narrative dogs — 7:176 the man who shed Allah's signs is debased to 'the likeness of the dog' that pants either way, while 18:18 the dog that kept company with the believing youths is ennobled, guarding their threshold inside Allah's protection; the same rare animal inverted around fidelity to the signs.

غور: 18:41 'aw yuṣbiḥa mā'uhā ghawran fa-lan tastaṭī'a lahu ṭalabā' ↔ 67:30 'in aṣbaḥa mā'ukum ghawran fa-man ya'tīkum bi-mā'in ma'īn' — the same rare aṣbaḥa + mā' + ghawran construction; the garden-parable's threat to one proud owner is generalized into al-Mulk's closing challenge to all.

توفيق: the noun occurs only in 4:62 and 11:88 — the hypocrites swear 'in aradnā illā iḥsānan wa-tawfīqā' while Shu'ayb declares 'in urīdu illā l-iṣlāḥa... wa-mā tawfīqī illā billāh': the identical exclusive in...illā claim of intending reform, false on the hypocrites' lips and true on the prophet's, who alone attributes tawfīq to Allah.

غمرة: 23:63 'bal qulūbuhum fī ghamratin min hādhā' — hearts submerged in a flood of heedlessness until We seize them ↔ 6:93 the wrongdoers 'fī ghamarāti l-mawt' as the angels stretch out their hands: the same drowning-flood image covering the heedless life and then closing over its end.

قلائد: 5:97 'ja'ala llāhu l-ka'bata l-bayta l-ḥarāma qiyāman lin-nāsi wa-sh-shahra l-ḥarāma wa-l-hadya wa-l-qalā'id' repeats verbatim the protected list of 5:2 'lā tuḥillū sha'ā'ira llāhi wa-lā sh-shahra l-ḥarāma wa-lā l-hadya wa-lā l-qalā'ida' and supplies its rationale — the surah's opening prohibition answered later by its own explanation of what these rites hold up.

سوّلت: Ya'qub's whole sentence 'bal sawwalat lakum anfusukum amran fa-ṣabrun jamīl' (12:18, over Yusuf's shirt) returns verbatim in 12:83 decades later over Binyamin — a designed refrain marking that the brothers' nafs is re-running the same script, and Ya'qub answering it with the same patience.

طاقة: the phrase 'lā ṭāqata lanā' occurs exactly twice in the Quran, both in al-Baqarah — 2:249 the deserters' defeatism 'lā ṭāqata lanā l-yawma bi-jālūta wa-junūdih' is inverted in the surah's closing du'a 2:286 'wa-lā tuḥammilnā mā lā ṭāqata lanā bihi': the same words of incapacity re-voiced as a prayer to the One who assigns capacity.

ميز: 3:179 'ḥattā yamīza l-khabītha mina ṭ-ṭayyib' ↔ 8:37 'li-yamīza llāhu l-khabītha mina ṭ-ṭayyib' — the identical rare clause: trials sift the corrupt from the pure among those claiming faith, and 8:37 carries the same sorting to its end, the khabīth piled up and cast into Jahannam.

ميز: the separation Allah promises in 3:179 ('He will not leave the believers as you are until He distinguishes the khabīth from the ṭayyib') is enacted on the Day in 36:59 'wa-mtāzū l-yawma ayyuhā l-mujrimūn' — the same root moving from Allah's promise to distinguish to His direct command to stand apart.

سخط: 3:162 'ka-man bā'a bi-sakhaṭin mina llāh' — returning laden with Allah's displeasure as one's acquisition ↔ 5:80 'la-bi'sa mā qaddamat lahum anfusuhum an sakhiṭa llāhu 'alayhim' — divine sakhaṭ as what one's own soul earns and sends ahead; both frame God's displeasure as a carried acquisition ending in the same abode of punishment.

سيل appears in Saba only at the two hinges of its gratitude diptych: 34:12 'asalnā lahu ʿayna l-qiṭr' — We made the spring of molten copper FLOW for grateful Sulaymān — and 34:16 'arsalnā ʿalayhim sayla l-ʿarim' — We sent the FLOOD of the dam against ungrateful Saba; the same rare root stages flow as gift and flow as judgment within one surah's argument.

زول as cosmic dislodgement: 35:41 'yumsiku s-samāwāti wa-l-arḍa an tazūlā... wa-la-in zālatā' — Allah holds the heavens and earth lest they slip from place — ↔ 14:46 'wa-in kāna makruhum li-tazūla minhu l-jibāl' — plotting so great mountains would slip; the same rare verb: what human scheming would dislodge, only Allah's grip keeps in place.

The rare epithet sā'iḥ appears only in the Quran's two believer-virtue catalogs: 9:112 'at-tā'ibūna l-ʿābidūna... as-sā'iḥūna' describing those who fulfilled the bayʿah, and 66:5 'tā'ibātin ʿābidātin sā'ihātin' describing the ideal wives — the same triple sequence (repentant, worshipping, sā'iḥ-) mirrored masculine to feminine across the two lists.

fatīl — the hair-thread in a date-stone's cleft — occurs only inside the fixed justice formula 'lā yuẓlamūna fatīlā': 17:71 seals the reading of one's own book (not a fiber docked), 4:49 seals Allah's sole authority over tazkiyah — the same micro-measure idiom deployed to declare divine reckoning exact.

The same rare formula 'wa-lā tuẓlamūna fatīlā' closes 4:77's answer to those who feared fighting — no sacrifice shortchanged by even the date-stone thread — echoing 17:71's courtroom guarantee that the book is read with not a fiber of injustice; fatīl exists in the Quran only inside this precision-of-justice formula.

rāgha — the fox's stealthy swerve — is used in the Quran exclusively of Ibrahim: 37:91/93 'fa-rāgha ilā ālihatihim... fa-rāgha ʿalayhim ḍarban' as he slips away to shatter the idols, and 51:26 'fa-rāgha ilā ahlihi' as he slips away to bring his guests the fattened calf — the same signature verb marking his quiet, decisive movement in both conviction and generosity.

The identical rare phrase 'min kulli zawjin bahīj' in the same argumentative role: 22:5 ends the resurrection proof ('if you are in doubt about the Resurrection... you see the earth lifeless... it brings forth every beautiful pair') and 50:7 answers the Quraysh's 'distant return' with the same earth that grows 'every beautiful pair' — beauty of regrown earth as the standing evidence of bodily return.

Near-identical phrase in twin creation-mercy catalogs: 21:31 'wa-jaʿalnā fīhā fijājan subulan laʿallahum yahtadūn' ↔ 71:20 'li-taslukū minhā subulan fijājan' — the same rare pairing of fijāj (mountain passes) with subul (ways), both as Allah's carved openings through the earth offered to people who then turn away.

The fajj as the God-carved route completed: 21:31 Allah places fijāj as ways 'that they might be guided,' and 22:27 the pilgrims answer Ibrahim's call 'min kulli fajjin ʿamīq' — from every deep pass; the rare noun's only other Quranic home, where the passes Allah opened become the roads to His House.

yuzjī — the shepherd's gentle-prodding verb — has exactly two active divine uses: 17:66 'rabbukumu lladhī yuzjī lakumu l-fulka fī l-baḥr' (He gently drives the ships through the sea for your provision) and 24:43 'anna llāha yuzjī saḥāban' (He gently drives the clouds toward rain); the same rare verb of soft providence moving great vessels of rizq through sea and sky.

The Quran's only two 'yamḥū Allāhu' clauses share one structure of divine erase-and-establish: 13:39 'yamḥū llāhu mā yashā'u wa-yuthbit' (He erases what He wills and confirms) ↔ 42:24 'wa-yamḥu llāhu l-bāṭila wa-yuḥiqqu l-ḥaqqa bi-kalimātih' (He erases falsehood and establishes truth) — the same verb paired each time with its affirming antonym as Allah's prerogative over what stands.

The identical rare dismissal 'aḍghāthu aḥlām' — a tangled fistful of dreams — spoken twice by those who cannot bear a true communication: the courtiers reduce the king's prophetic dream to jumble in 12:44, and the deniers reduce the Quran itself to jumble in 21:5; Yusuf's narrative proves the phrase wrong, exposing the same dismissal when aimed at revelation.

ṣarḥ occurs in the Quran only in two royal scenes: Bilqis enters Sulayman's glass ṣarḥ, discovers her certain eyes deceived her, and submits — 'aslamtu maʿa Sulaymāna li-llāh' (27:44) — while Pharaoh orders Haman to build a ṣarḥ of fired clay to 'look at the God of Musa' and calls him a liar (28:38); the same rare tower-word staging two monarchs' opposite responses to the unseen God — humbled perception versus self-deifying ascent.

The second telling of Pharaoh's ṣarḥ (40:36 'ibni lī ṣarḥan laʿallī ablughu l-asbāb... wa-innī la-aẓunnuhu kādhibā') completes the Quran's only-two-ṣarḥs contrast with 27:44: Bilqis's ṣarḥ moment ends in 'I have wronged myself, I submit,' Pharaoh's in tabāb (ruin) — the rare word marks the tower as the test-site of a sovereign's posture before the true God.

نسخ as divine act: 2:106 'whatever āyah We abrogate (نَنسَخْ)... We bring better' ↔ 22:52 'Allah abrogates (فَيَنسَخُ) what Shaytan casts, then makes His āyāt firm' — the only two verbal uses of Allah performing naskh, both asserting sovereign editing of revelation-content that ends in firmer āyāt.

شُحّ, the Quran's rare word for ingrained avarice: 59:9 crowns the Ansar — 'whoever is shielded from شُحَّ نَفْسِهِ, they are the successful' — while 33:19 brands the Trench hypocrites أَشِحَّةً عَلَيْكُمْ... أَشِحَّةً عَلَى ٱلْخَيْرِ; the same rare noun paints the exact anti-portrait in the same Madinan community-crisis discourse.

دكك — what divine decree does to the most solid things at the appointed time: 18:98 Dhul-Qarnayn says of his iron wall 'when the promise of my Lord comes He will make it دَكَّآء' ↔ 69:14 the earth and mountains are 'دُكَّتَا دَكَّةً وَٰحِدَةً' at the Blast — the wall's promised leveling is a preview of the same eschatological dakk.

Thamud's carving retold: 7:74 'تَنْحِتُونَ ٱلْجِبَالَ بُيُوتًا' ↔ 15:82 'يَنْحِتُونَ مِنَ ٱلْجِبَالِ بُيُوتًا ءَامِنِينَ' — the same people, the same mountain-carved homes, the same engineered security that the cry/quake strips away.

نزغ — Shaytan's prick that manufactures discord: 41:36 'وَإِمَّا يَنزَغَنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلشَّيْطَـٰنِ نَزْغٌ فَٱسْتَعِذْ' names the mechanism and its cure ↔ 12:100 Yusuf diagnoses his whole family rupture with the same rare verb, 'مِنۢ بَعْدِ أَن نَّزَغَ ٱلشَّيْطَـٰنُ بَيْنِى وَبَيْنَ إِخْوَتِى' — the lived case of the prick 41:36 warns about.

نزغ with Shaytan as sole agent: 41:36 commands isti'adha against the نَزْغ that arrives at the threshold of doing the better thing ↔ 17:53 grounds the command to 'say what is best' in the same diagnosis, 'إِنَّ ٱلشَّيْطَـٰنَ يَنزَغُ بَيْنَهُمْ' — speech is where the prick enters between people.

جسد — the Quran's word for body-minus-life: 20:88 the calf is 'جَسَدًا لَّهُ خُوَارٌ', a body counterfeiting life with a sound ↔ 21:8 'وَمَا جَعَلْنَـٰهُمْ جَسَدًا لَّا يَأْكُلُونَ ٱلطَّعَامَ' — prophets are precisely NOT mere jasad; the rare noun draws the same line between hollow body and living agent from both sides.

نفد theologizing the exhaustible vs the divine: 18:109 the sea as ink 'لَنَفِدَ ٱلْبَحْرُ' before the Lord's words 'تَنفَدَ' ↔ 16:96 'مَا عِندَكُمْ يَنفَدُ وَمَا عِندَ ٱللَّهِ بَاقٍ' — the same rare verb drawing the identical line: created stock runs out, what is with Allah does not.

نفد denied of what is Allah's: 18:109 His words outlast the sea-ink that runs out ↔ 38:54 Paradise provision is 'لَرِزْقُنَا مَا لَهُ مِن نَّفَادٍ' — the root's noun form used once in the Quran, precisely to negate depletion of what Allah gives, completing the motif the ink-verses state for His speech.

The wing-lowering idiom, found only three times in the Quran: 15:88 commands the Prophet 'وَٱخْفِضْ جَنَاحَكَ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ' ↔ 17:24 commands the child 'وَٱخْفِضْ لَهُمَا جَنَاحَ ٱلذُّلِّ مِنَ ٱلرَّحْمَةِ' toward aged parents — the same rare posture of deliberate tenderness transferred from prophet-to-community to child-to-parents.

شَيْخٌ كَبِيرٌ occurs exactly twice in the Quran, both times in a child's plea before a powerful stranger invoking an incapacitated aged father: 28:23 the Madyan daughters explain to Musa 'وَأَبُونَا شَيْخٌ كَبِيرٌ' ↔ 12:78 the brothers plead to Yusuf 'إِنَّ لَهُۥٓ أَبًا شَيْخًا كَبِيرًا فَخُذْ أَحَدَنَا مَكَانَهُ' — the same rare epithet doing the same narrative work in the Quran's two great mirror-narratives of Yusuf and Musa.

مُسْتَوْدَع occurs only twice in the Quran and both times paired with مُسْتَقَرّ: 6:98 humanity from one soul, 'فَمُسْتَقَرٌّ وَمُسْتَوْدَعٌ' ↔ 11:6 every creature's provision is on Allah, 'وَيَعْلَمُ مُسْتَقَرَّهَا وَمُسْتَوْدَعَهَا' — the same settled-place/deposited-place merism inside twin catalogues of Allah's exhaustive knowledge, each sealed with 'in a clear Book'.

The identical predicate يُنَزِّلُ ٱلْغَيْثَ appears only in these two ayahs: 31:34 places the ghayth among the five things whose knowledge is with Allah alone ↔ 42:28 'He sends down the ghayth after they have despaired' — the despair exists precisely because the relief-rain's timing is the ghayb 31:34 reserves for Him; two halves of one theology of divinely-timed relief.

The gold house in both: 17:93 the deniers demand 'بَيْتٌ مِّن زُخْرُفٍ' as the price of belief ↔ 43:33-35 Allah answers the same economy — He would give the disbelievers houses with silver roofs 'وَزُخْرُفًا', for all of it is mere 'مَتَـٰعُ ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا'; the identical house-of-gold image is demanded in one surah and devalued in the other.

زخرف as dunya's deceptive gilding: 10:24 the earth 'أَخَذَتِ ٱلْأَرْضُ زُخْرُفَهَا وَٱزَّيَّنَتْ' at the very moment before the command mows it down ↔ 43:35 zukhruf dismissed as passing matāʿ of the lower life against the ākhirah — the same rare noun marking splendor whose peak is proof of its worthlessness.

The idhān (oily compromise) idiom occurs only in these two places: 68:9 'وَدُّوا۟ لَوْ تُدْهِنُ فَيُدْهِنُونَ' — they wish you would grease your stance so they could grease theirs ↔ 56:81 'أَفَبِهَـٰذَا ٱلْحَدِيثِ أَنتُم مُّدْهِنُونَ' — is it THIS discourse you meet with oiled evasion? The same Form-IV metaphor of softening one's stand toward the revelation, as pressure on the Prophet and as indictment of the deniers.

مدرارا (midrāran) occurs only three times in the Quran, always in the formula 'sent the sky upon them/you in torrents': 71:11 (and 11:52) is the prophetic promise — istighfar opens the sky in midrār — while 6:6 shows the same مدرارا already granted to destroyed generations who sinned under it; promise and cautionary tale share one rare formula.

سراج: 25:61 hangs a sirāj (sun) and a qamar munīr in the sky; 33:46 names the Prophet ﷺ سراجا منيرا — fusing the sun's epithet with the moon's, transferring the cosmic lamp deliberately onto the Messenger as the burning source of guidance-light.

السموم — Hell's pore-penetrating scorching wind — appears as punishment only in these two passages, as mirrored panels: 56:42 the Companions of the Left are IN samūm and ḥamīm, 52:27 the people of Paradise recall being protected FROM عذاب السموم; the same rare word names the fate one group suffers and the other is spared.

ينسلون occurs only twice, in the same 'من X ينسلون' frame and both in end-times scenes: 21:96 Gog and Magog 'from every height they pour down' and 36:51 the dead 'from the graves to their Lord they pour out' — the same verb of swift swarming marks the two great eschatological release-scenes.

أرذل العمر: 16:70 'ومنكم من يرد إلى أرذل العمر لكي لا يعلم بعد علم شيئا' and 22:5 'ومنكم من يرد إلى أرذل العمر لكيلا يعلم من بعد علم شيئا' — a near-verbatim twin clause on being returned to the most decrepit age, deployed in both surahs as proof of Allah's total control over the life-cycle and hence the resurrection.

داخر vs استكبار in both: 16:48-49 all creation prostrates وهم داخرون and the angels لا يستكبرون, while 40:60 those who يستكبرون عن عبادتي will enter Jahannam داخرين — the same rare word marks willing lowliness in creation and forced abasement for the arrogant who refused it.

داخرين: 27:87 on the trumpet-Day 'وكل أتوه داخرين' — all come to Him abased — and 40:60 the ones too proud to supplicate 'سيدخلون جهنم داخرين'; the same rare participle names the compulsory abasement of the Return.

داخرون: 37:18 answers the resurrection-mockers 'قل نعم وأنتم داخرون' — you will be raised utterly abased — the same reversal 40:60 decrees for those who scorned worship, arrogance now traded for dukhūr then.

The sky as a built roof: 21:32 'وجعلنا السماء سقفا محفوظا' (the protected ceiling as mercy-argument) and 52:5 'والسقف المرفوع' (the raised ceiling sworn by as witness) — the same rare architectural reframing of the sky as the roof of the human house.

لمز: 9:58 'ومنهم من يلمزك في الصدقات' — the hypocrites jab the Prophet over charity distribution — and 104:1 'ويل لكل همزة لمزة' condemns the person who has become that jab; the surah of the fault-finder names the character whose behavior At-Tawbah documents.

لمز: 9:79 'الذين يلمزون المطوعين من المؤمنين في الصدقات... فيسخرون منهم' — jabbing both the generous and the poor giver — is the lived scene of 104:1's لمزة, the habitual fault-finder whose cut Allah answers with سخر الله منهم and woe.

عفف paired with غنى in both: 2:273 the poor are mistaken for rich 'أغنياء من التعفف' — restraint reads as wealth — and 4:6 'ومن كان غنيا فليستعفف' — actual wealth obligates restraint from orphan property; the root and the ghinā-axis travel together in both rulings.

عفف with غنى again: 24:33 'وليستعفف الذين لا يجدون نكاحا حتى يغنيهم الله من فضله' — restraint practiced until Allah grants ghinā — mirrors 2:273 where التعفف itself makes the destitute look أغنياء; both texts define isti'fāf as dignity that anticipates or substitutes for wealth from Allah.

طرد: Nuh refuses the elite's price — 'وما أنا بطارد الذين آمنوا... من ينصرني من الله إن طردتهم' (11:29-30) — and the same demand recurs against Muhammad ﷺ: 'ولا تطرد الذين يدعون ربهم... فتطردهم فتكون من الظالمين' (6:52); the identical verb, the identical elite pressure to expel poor believers, the identical warning of ẓulm.

تركن occurs only twice in the Quran, both warning against inclining toward the unjust: 11:113 'ولا تركنوا إلى الذين ظلموا فتمسكم النار' and 17:74 'ولولا أن ثبتناك لقد كدت تركن إليهم شيئا قليلا' — the standing command and the Prophet's near-miss under pressure, each followed by the threat of fire/doubled punishment with no helper besides Allah.

The same event in the same formula: 37:76 'ونجيناه وأهله من الكرب العظيم' and 21:76 'فنجيناه وأهله من الكرب العظيم' — Nuh's rescue from the great karb, retold with near-identical wording in both surahs.

كرب travels only with najjā in the Quran: the rescue-formula نجينا من الكرب العظيم (37:76 Nuh, 37:115 Musa and Harun) is universalized in 6:64 — 'قل الله ينجيكم منها ومن كل كرب' — the same rare noun extended from the prophets' great distress to every distress of everyone who calls.

The identical clause as counterfactual and as history: 8:43 (Badr) 'لو أراكهم كثيرا لفشلتم وتنازعتم في الأمر' — what would have happened — and 3:152 (Uhud) 'حتى إذا فشلتم وتنازعتم في الأمر وعصيتم' — what did happen; the fashal+tanāzu' pair is verbatim across the two battle surahs.

8:46 legislates the exact mechanism Uhud exposed: 'ولا تنازعوا فتفشلوا وتذهب ريحكم' — dispute produces fashal — while 3:152 records that sequence occurring (فشلتم وتنازعتم) and costing the victory; command and case study of one root.

Within the Uhud narrative the root frames the arc: 3:122 'إذ همت طائفتان منكم أن تفشلا والله وليهما' — the near-fashal Allah restrained at the battle's morning — and 3:152 the fashal that later broke through at the archers' pass; the same word measures the distance between the temptation and the fall.

كسف: Quraysh demand 'تُسْقِطَ السماءَ كما زعمتَ علينا كِسَفًا' (17:92) exactly as Shu'ayb's people taunted 'فأسقط علينا كسفا من السماء' (26:187) — the same drop-sky-fragments-on-us challenge placed in two deniers' mouths, and in 26 it is answered by the Day of the Shadow.

كسف: the demand 'make the sky fall on us in kisaf' (17:92) is met by the divine counter-threat 'أو نُسْقِطْ عليهم كِسَفًا من السماء' (34:9) — same rare noun with the same verb أسقط, human taunt and divine warning built from one formula.

قِطْر (molten copper): Allah made 'عين القِطر' flow for Sulayman (34:12) and Dhul-Qarnayn pours 'قِطرا' over the fired iron barrier (18:96) — the Quran's only two uses of qiṭr, both God-granted mastery of molten metal in the hands of a righteous ruler-builder.

وسوس: 'فوسوس لهما الشيطان' (7:20) is the first enacted case of exactly what An-Nas names in the abstract — 'الوسواس الخناس الذي يوسوس في صدور الناس' (114:4-5); the Garden's whisper generalized into the permanent mechanism the Quran closes by seeking refuge from.

وسوس: 'ما تُوَسْوِسُ به نفسُه' (50:16) and 'يوسوس في صدور الناس' (114:5) — the same rare verb locating the whisper inside the chest/nafs, mapping the two sources (the self and the whisperer) of one inner voice.

جاثمين: Thamud's end 'فأخذتهم الرجفة فأصبحوا في دارهم جاثمين' (7:78) is the identical clause that closes Madyan's account in 29:37 — the Quran's fixed death-posture formula for the morning after denial, sealing each destroyed people motionless in their homes.

جاثمين: 'فأصبحوا في ديارهم جاثمين' (11:67, Thamud seized by the ṣayḥah) repeats verbatim the closing clause of 29:37 (Madyan seized by the rajfah) — the same rare participle used as the signature freeze-frame of divine punishment.

سرح: Al-Baqarah legislates 'تسريحٌ بإحسان' / 'سرِّحوهن بمعروف' (2:229, 2:231) as the law of every marital exit; 33:28's 'أُسرِّحْكُنَّ سراحا جميلا' applies the same rare release-idiom to the Prophet's own household in the verses of choice — release-with-beauty as a rule that binds even the highest house.

'خاوية على عروشها': the generalized ruin-formula of 22:45 ('فهي خاوية على عروشها') is the very phrase describing the town the man passed in 2:259 ('وهي خاوية على عروشها') — the same three-word collapse image, once as a rule of history, once as the scene that provokes the resurrection question.

'خاوية على عروشها': the rich man's garden 'وهي خاوية على عروشها' (18:42) repeats verbatim the fallen-town formula of 22:45 — one collapse-image deliberately spanning a private garden and whole wrongdoing civilizations.

برد negated in Hell: 'وظل من يحموم لا بارد ولا كريم' (56:43-44) and 'لا يذوقون فيها بردا ولا شرابا إلا حميما' (78:24-25) — both portraits deny the transgressors the same coolness and supply the same ḥamīm; absence-of-bard is the shared signature of the punishment.

ربط على القلب: 'وربطنا على قلوبهم إذ قاموا' (18:14, the cave youths' public stand) and 'وليربط على قلوبكم ويثبت به الأقدام' (8:11, the night before Badr) — the identical rare idiom of Allah binding hearts firm at the moment of mortal danger.

'فهم يوزعون': 'ويوم يُحشر أعداء الله إلى النار فهم يوزعون' (41:19) and 'ويوم نحشر من كل أمة فوجا ممن يكذب بآياتنا فهم يوزعون' (27:83) — the same yawm + ḥashr + yūzaʿūn formula for the deniers marshaled in ranks toward judgment.

مبلسون: 'أخذناهم بغتة فإذا هم مبلسون' (6:44) is the worldly rehearsal of 'وهم فيه مبلسون' (43:75) — the same rare term for despair at the instant punishment closes, first at a nation's sudden seizure, finally inside unrelieved Hell.

مبلسون: 'فتحنا عليهم بابا ذا عذاب شديد إذا هم فيه مبلسون' (23:77) and 'لا يُفتَّر عنهم وهم فيه مبلسون' (43:75) — near-identical clauses (فيه مبلسون) of terminal despair inside punishment that will not relent.

iblās: 'يُبلس المجرمون' when the Hour stands (30:12) and 'إن المجرمين... وهم فيه مبلسون' (43:74-75) — the same rare verb with the same subject al-mujrimūn, the Hour's stunned silence hardening into Hell's permanent despair.

رحل (saddlebag): 12:62 Yusuf orders 'put their merchandise in their riḥāl' as a hidden mercy that draws the brothers back ↔ 12:70/75 'he placed the cup in his brother's raḥl... whoever's raḥl it is found in' — the same secret-planting-in-the-raḥl device repeated deliberately, first as lure, then as the plan Allah 'kidnā' for Yusuf.

ضاقت عليهم/عليكم الأرض بِمَا رَحُبَتْ — 'the earth closed in despite its raḥb (vastness)' occurs only twice in the Quran, both in At-Tawbah: 9:25 the army at Hunayn after trusting its numbers, 9:118 the three left behind after Tabuk — the same constriction formula, each time resolved by Allah's tawbah/sakīnah (9:27, 9:118).

لجّ (to persist obstinately): 23:75 'even if We showed them mercy and removed their harm, la-lajjū fī ṭughyānihim' ↔ 67:21 'bal lajjū fī ʿutuwwin wa-nufūr' — the verb's only two occurrences, both diagnosing the heart that persists in rebellion no matter what Allah sends.

غضّ of the voice: 31:19 Luqman's 'wa-ghḍuḍ min ṣawtika' (lower your voice) ↔ 49:3 'yaghuḍḍūna aṣwātahum ʿinda rasūli-llāh' — the only two voice-lowering uses of this rare verb, the father's adab-counsel become the community's adab before the Messenger.

لين (softness in prophetic address): 20:44 Musa is commanded 'fa-qūlā lahu qawlan layyinan' even toward Pharaoh ↔ 3:159 'fa-bimā raḥmatin mina-llāhi linta lahum' — the Prophet's gentleness with the failing Uhud community; the same rare root making softness the divinely-mandated register of prophetic leadership, toward tyrant and follower alike.

The exact phrase مَا عَنِتُّمْ occurs only twice: 3:118 the inner-circle enemies 'waddū mā ʿanittum' (they long for your distress) ↔ 9:128 the Messenger 'ʿazīzun ʿalayhi mā ʿanittum' (your distress weighs heavily on him) — the same phrase with inverted bearers, enmity that craves the believers' ʿanat against the prophetic heart pained by it.

عنت and the Messenger among the believers: 9:128 'a Messenger min anfusikum — grievous to him is your ʿanat' ↔ 49:7 'among you is the Messenger of Allah; if he obeyed you in much of the matter la-ʿanittum' — twin Medinan statements that the Messenger's presence and independence shield the community from its own ʿanat.

The identical clause وَجَاوَزْنَا بِبَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ ٱلْبَحْرَ opens both passages — its only two occurrences: 10:90 continues into Pharaoh's too-late confession at the drowning point, 7:138 into Israel's 'make for us a god' immediately after deliverance — two retellings of the sea crossing, each exposing what the crossing did not fix.

أسف as prophetic grief at one's own people: 7:150 Musa returns 'ghaḍbāna asifan' to the calf his people made ↔ 12:84 Yaʿqub turns away crying 'yā asafā ʿalā Yūsuf' at what his sons did — the same rare grief-word for a prophet wounded by the betrayal of his closest kin.

أسف: 7:150 Musa's 'ghaḍbāna asifan' at his people's apostasy ↔ 18:6 the Prophet ﷺ 'bākhiʿun nafsaka... asafan' — nearly destroying himself in grief over his people's rejection; the root's rare occurrences consistently mark the prophet's grief over those he was sent to.

كَٱلْمُهْلِ — the same rare simile of molten dregs for Hell's sustenance: 18:29 relief-water 'like muhl that scalds the faces' ↔ 44:45 Zaqqum 'like muhl boiling in the bellies' — the drink and the food of the Fire cast in one deliberately repeated image.

The amānah-rendering command stated twice with the same verb: 4:58 'inna Allāha yaʾmurukum an tuʾaddū al-amānāti ilā ahlihā' ↔ 2:283 'fal-yuʾaddi alladhī uʾtumina amānatahu' — the general civilizational command and its application inside the debt/pledge legislation.

ʿalā al-arāʾik: 76:13 'muttakiʾīna fīhā ʿalā al-arāʾik' beyond sun and cold ↔ 83:23 'ʿalā al-arāʾiki yanẓurūn' — the same rare couch-word in the Quran's fixed paradise scene of enthroned rest, here bearing the radiant gaze of the abrār.

ʿalā al-arāʾik: 76:13 the abrār reclining on the arāʾik ↔ 83:35 'ʿalā al-arāʾiki yanẓurūn' — the couch of rest becomes the seat of the restored gaze, the once-mocked believers looking down on their mockers from the same arāʾik.

The same prohibition clause وَمَا أُهِلَّ لِغَيْرِ ٱللَّهِ بِهِ with the same four-item list (carrion, blood, swine, what is dedicated to other than Allah) and the same necessity exception (fa-mani-ḍṭurra... ghafūrun raḥīm): 5:3 the perfected-religion statement ↔ 16:115 the same ruling inside An-Nahl's warning against inventing halal and haram.

عصر brackets Yusuf's prison-dream arc: 12:36 the cupbearer dreams 'arānī aʿṣiru khamran' (I press wine) ↔ 12:49 Yusuf's interpretation of the king's dream ends 'ʿāmun fīhi yughāthu an-nāsu wa-fīhi yaʿṣirūn' — the year of relief sealed with the cupbearer's own pressing-verb, dream and fulfillment tied by the same rare root.

The bones-clothed-with-flesh image occurs only twice: 23:14 'fa-kasawnā al-ʿiẓāma laḥman' in the embryonic assembly line ↔ 2:259 'wa-nẓur ilā al-ʿiẓāmi kayfa nunshizuhā thumma naksūhā laḥman' in the hundred-year resurrection proof — the same rare metaphor deliberately reused so that resurrection replays the first creation before the watcher's eyes.

وسط as excellence-in-the-middle: 2:143 أُمَّةً وَسَطًا (the Prophet glossed wasaṭ as al-'adl — just/best) ↔ 2:238 ٱلصَّلَوٰةِ ٱلْوُسْطَىٰ, the fuʿlā elative of the same root naming the middle/best prayer — the middle nation guards the middle prayer, a lexical pairing the classical lexicons and both tadabbur files draw explicitly.

فرد as eschatological solitude: 6:94 'you have come to Us furādā as We created you the first time,' stripped of wealth and imagined intercessors ↔ 19:80 'We inherit from him what he claims wa-ya'tīnā fardan' — the same stripping of the man who boasted of wealth and children.

6:94's 'laqad ji'tumūnā furādā kamā khalaqnākum awwala marrah' is universalized in 19:95 'wa-kulluhum ātīhi yawma l-qiyāmati fardan' — every creature comes to Him alone; the Maryam tadabbur itself reads fardan as the letter-for-letter word of 19:80 made a universal condition, and 6:94 is its most developed statement.

Ghafir deploys maqt twice as its own thread: 40:10 defines it — لَمَقْتُ ٱللَّهِ أَكْبَرُ مِن مَّقْتِكُمْ أَنفُسَكُمْ, divine loathing greater than the damned's self-loathing — and 40:35 applies it, كَبُرَ مَقْتًا عِندَ ٱللَّهِ, to those who dispute His signs, the very clause echoed verbatim at 61:3.

The same verb of warping truth: 3:78 يَلْوُۥنَ أَلْسِنَتَهُم بِٱلْكِتَـٰبِ — bending tongues with the Book so forgery sounds like scripture ↔ 4:135 وَإِن تَلْوُۥٓا۟ أَوْ تُعْرِضُوا۟ — twisting testimony away from justice; scripture-reading and witness-bearing corrupted by the identical act of layy.

The fixed pair ٱلْعَدَٰوَةَ وَٱلْبَغْضَآءَ as an intra-Maidah counterpoint: 5:64 'We cast (alqaynā) enmity and baghḍā' among them until the Day of Resurrection' as punishment for covenant-breakers ↔ 5:91 'Satan only wants to cast (yūqi'a) enmity and baghḍā' among you through khamr and maysir' — what Allah decreed for them, Satan schemes for the believers.

The same word-pair, inverted in agency: 5:64 Allah casts al-'adāwa wal-baghḍā' among them until al-qiyāmah ↔ 60:4 Ibrahim and those with him declare 'badā baynanā wa-baynakumu l-'adāwatu wal-baghḍā'u abadan ḥattā tu'minū' — the formulaic couple marking enmity that only tawhid can lift.

A designed antithesis on one rare word: 18:29 closes Hell's scene with بِئْسَ ٱلشَّرَابُ وَسَآءَتْ مُرْتَفَقًا and 18:31 closes Paradise's with نِعْمَ ٱلثَّوَابُ وَحَسُنَتْ مُرْتَفَقًا — al-Tabari (cited in the 18:31 tadabbur) reads the second murtafaq as deliberately answering the first: the false resting place versus the true one.

The maḥīṣ formula of no-escape: 42:35 'those who dispute Our signs may know mā lahum min maḥīṣ' ↔ 4:121 Satan's promise-fed followers 'lā yajidūna 'anhā maḥīṣan' from Jahannam — the same rare noun sealing the end of every evasive strategy, argument or false hope.

Verbatim clause: 42:35 مَا لَهُم مِّن مَّحِيصٍ for those who dispute Allah's signs ↔ 41:48 مَا لَهُم مِّن مَّحِيصٍ when the gods they called upon have strayed from them — in both, a lifetime of evasion hardens into the certainty that there is no place to swerve to.

ḥāmiyah as Hell's reserved epithet: 101:11 answers 'wa-mā adrāka mā hiyah?' with نَارٌ حَامِيَةٌۢ, and 88:4 gives the only other occurrence — تَصْلَىٰ نَارًا حَامِيَةً — both in short Makkan Day-scenes where humbled faces/light scales meet the same scorching Fire.

muṣfarran — the yellowing of vegetation as the test of the heart: 57:20's dunya-parable 'thumma yahīju fa-tarāhu muṣfarran thumma yakūnu ḥuṭāman' ↔ 30:51 'wa-la'in arsalnā rīḥan fa-ra'awhu muṣfarran la-ẓallū min ba'dihi yakfurūn' — the same rare Form-IX participle, the same withered crop, exposing gratitude that was conditional on the harvest.

The identical refrain وَلَا تَعْثَوْا۟ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مُفْسِدِينَ: Shu'ayb's charter to Madyan (11:85) and Musa's people at the twelve springs (2:60) — in both, the command follows granted provision (honest trade / eat and drink of Allah's rizq), tying consumption to restraint from corruption.

The same closing formula wa-lā ta'thaw fī l-arḍi mufsidīn on two prophets' tongues: Shu'ayb to Madyan (11:85) and Salih to Thamud (7:74) — each after reminding the people of how Allah settled and enriched them in the land.

Two tellings of the same Shu'ayb sermon: 11:85 'awfū l-mikyāla wal-mīzāna bil-qisṭi wa-lā tabkhasū n-nāsa ashyā'ahum wa-lā ta'thaw fī l-arḍi mufsidīn' ↔ 26:181-183 repeats full measure, the straight balance, lā tabkhasū n-nāsa ashyā'ahum, and the identical wa-lā ta'thaw clause.

The executed ḥāṣib and its standing threat: 54:34 'innā arsalnā 'alayhim ḥāṣiban' on Lut's people ↔ 17:68 'do you feel secure that He will not... yursila 'alaykum ḥāṣiban' — the historical stone-storm turned into a question aimed at the sea-rescued ingrate, paired in both warning verses with khasf (the earth swallowing).

The same irsāl + ḥāṣib construction: 54:34's narrative 'arsalnā 'alayhim ḥāṣiban illā āla Lūṭ' is the very entry itemized in 29:40's catalogue of ruin — 'fa-minhum man arsalnā 'alayhi ḥāṣiban' — alongside the ṣayḥah, the khasf, and the drowning.

54:34's ḥāṣib sent on Lut's people is the precedent behind 67:17's 'am amintum man fī s-samā'i an yursila 'alaykum ḥāṣiban' — the same verb-object pair (yursila... ḥāṣiban), and like 17:68 the threat is coupled with the earth's khasf one breath earlier.

Executed versus threatened divine effacement: 54:37 فَطَمَسْنَآ أَعْيُنَهُمْ — Lut's assailants' eyes erased on the spot ↔ 4:47 مِّن قَبْلِ أَن نَّطْمِسَ وُجُوهًا فَنَرُدَّهَا عَلَىٰٓ أَدْبَارِهَا — the same verb warning the People of the Book of faces effaced and turned backwards; the one carried-out ṭams is the proof behind the warning.

The same confrontation carried by the same rare word: 26:70-71 Ibrahim asks his father and people 'mā ta'budūn?' and they confess نَعْبُدُ أَصْنَامًا ↔ 6:74 Ibrahim to Azar: أَتَتَّخِذُ أَصْنَامًا ءَالِهَةً — the aṣnām dialogue that opens both tellings of his break with his people.

Word to deed in one narrative arc: the aṣnām interrogation of 26:69-76 ('do they hear you when you call?') is the argument whose action-sequel is 21:57-58 — 'wa-tallāhi la-akīdanna أَصْنَٰمَكُم' and the smashing to fragments; the same scene, the same word, debate become demolition.

The arc's resolution: the young Ibrahim who interrogated his people's aṣnām-worship (26:71) later prays وَٱجْنُبْنِى وَبَنِىَّ أَن نَّعْبُدَ ٱلْأَصْنَامَ (14:35) — the identical word na'budu + aṣnām, now feared for his own descendants because 'they have led many people astray.'

The only two aṣnām + 'ākifīn collocations in the Quran: 26:71 'na'budu aṣnāman fa-naẓallu lahā عَٰكِفِينَ' ↔ 7:138 a people يَعْكُفُونَ عَلَىٰٓ أَصْنَامٍ لَّهُمْ whom Bani Israil immediately want to imitate — the same clinging devotion, confessed by Ibrahim's people and coveted by Musa's.

The precedent of the ancients 'has passed': 8:38 فَقَدْ مَضَتْ سُنَّتُ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ warning those who return to hostility ↔ 43:8 وَمَضَىٰ مَثَلُ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ after mightier mockers were destroyed — the only two places where maḍā governs al-awwalīn, turning past destruction into a standing legal precedent.

خوّل (khawwala, to grant as stewardship): 39:49 'when We bestow on him a favor (khawwalnāhu) he says I was only given it for my knowledge' ↔ 6:94 'you have left behind what We bestowed on you (mā khawwalnākum)' — the same rare verb frames blessings as revocable grants that man misattributes in life and must abandon at death.

يحرّفون (yuḥarrifūn): 2:75 'a group of them hear the word of Allah then distort it after understanding it, knowingly' ↔ 5:13 'they distort the words from their proper places (yuḥarrifūna al-kalima ʿan mawāḍiʿihi)' — the same Form-II verb naming the same crime of scriptural taḥrīf by the same community.

يحرّفون (yuḥarrifūn): 2:75 distortion of Allah's word after comprehension ↔ 5:41 'they distort words from their places, saying: if you are given this take it, if not beware' — 5:41 dramatizes in a live outcome-shopping scene the very taḥrīf mechanism 2:75-79 diagnoses.

صمّ بكم عمي: 2:18 'deaf, dumb, blind — they will not return' (hypocrites in the storm) ↔ 2:171 'deaf, dumb, blind — they do not understand' (blind followers as livestock) — the identical three-word formula closing both parables of failed reception within the same surah.

بكم (bukm): 2:18 'deaf, dumb, blind — they will not return' ↔ 8:22 'the worst of creatures before Allah are the deaf and dumb who do not reason' — the same rare epithet-pair upgraded from parable to divine verdict on those who say we heard while not hearing.

فخور (fakhūr): 57:23 'Allah does not love every mukhtāl fakhūr' as the cure for exulting over what He gave ↔ 31:18 Luqman's 'Allah does not love every mukhtāl fakhūr' against strutting — the identical rare divine-disapproval formula applied once to the heart's exultation and once to the body's gait.

فخر within one surah's arc: 57:20 defines dunya as 'tafākhur baynakum' (mutual boasting) and three ayahs later 57:23 prescribes the antidote — the pre-written Register so that none exults, 'Allah loves not every mukhtāl fakhūr' — diagnosis and cure carried by the same root.

أحبار (aḥbār, rabbis): 5:44 the aḥbār judge by the Torah 'by what they were entrusted to preserve of the Book of Allah' ↔ 9:31 'they took their aḥbār and monks as lords besides Allah' — the same rare title marks the trust and its inversion: guardians of revelation become objects of obedience-worship.

أحبار (aḥbār): 5:63 'why do the rabbāniyyūn and aḥbār not forbid their sinful speech and consuming of unlawful gain?' ↔ 9:31 the people take those same aḥbār as lords — the silent scholars of 5:63 are precisely the class 9:31 says usurped Allah's legislative right.

أحبار (aḥbār): 9:31 'they took their aḥbār and monks as lords' is immediately grounded by 9:34 'many of the aḥbār and monks consume people's wealth unjustly and bar from Allah's path' — the same pair (aḥbār wa-ruhbān) in consecutive passages, lordship exposed as economic exploitation.

أسرى (asrā, captives): 8:67 'it is not for a prophet to have captives until he subdues the land' ↔ 8:70 'O Prophet, say to the captives in your hands: if Allah knows good in your hearts He will give you better than what was taken' — one continuous Badr-captives scene: the ruling to the believers, then the address to the captives themselves.

مناسك (manāsik): 2:128 Ibrahim at the House prays 'arinā manāsikanā' (show us our rites) ↔ 2:200 'when you have completed your manāsik, remember Allah' — the dua asked while raising the foundations is answered in the same surah's hajj legislation: the rites requested are the rites legislated.

منسك (mansak): 2:128 Ibrahim asks 'show us our manāsik' ↔ 22:34 'for every community We appointed a mansak, that they mention Allah's name over the livestock He provided' — Surah al-Hajj universalizes what Ibrahim requested at the House, in a passage that itself sits inside the surah's Ibrahim-and-Kaaba sequence.

منسك (mansak): 2:128 'arinā manāsikanā' at the founding of the House ↔ 22:67 'for every nation We appointed a mansak they are to perform, so let them not contend with you' — the rite Ibrahim asked to be shown becomes the argument that rites are divinely appointed, not grounds for quarrel.

أفرغ علينا صبرًا: 7:126 the sorcerers facing Firʿawn's crucifixion threat pray 'rabbanā afrigh ʿalaynā ṣabran wa-tawaffanā muslimīn' ↔ 2:250 Talut's small band facing Jalut prays 'rabbanā afrigh ʿalaynā ṣabran wa-thabbit aqdāmanā' — the Quran's only two occurrences of this dua-formula, both on the lips of a believing few before overwhelming tyrant power, asking for patience to be POURED like liquid.

بروج (burūj, constellations): 15:16 'We placed burūj in the sky and beautified it for the onlookers' ↔ 85:1 the oath 'wa-s-samāʾi dhāti l-burūj' opening the surah named for them — the same rare sky-of-constellations image, stated as creative act in al-Hijr and invoked as cosmic witness over the persecuted believers in al-Buruj.

قست قلوبهم: 2:74 'then your hearts hardened after that, like stones or harder' after witnessing resurrection ↔ 6:43 'but their hearts hardened (qasat qulūbuhum) and Shaytan beautified their deeds' when affliction should have humbled them — the same verb marking hearts that harden precisely under what should soften them.

قسو: 2:74 Banū Isrāʾīl's hearts 'became like stones or harder in qaswah' ↔ 57:16 warns the believers 'be not like those given the Book before, the term grew long over them fa-qasat qulūbuhum' — 57:16 explicitly holds up the hardened-heart history of 2:74 as the fate believers must avoid.

قنط (qunūṭ, despair of mercy): 39:53 'lā taqnaṭū min raḥmati llāh — do not despair of Allah's mercy, He forgives all sins' ↔ 15:56 Ibrahim: 'wa-man yaqnaṭu min raḥmati rabbihi illā ḍ-ḍāllūn — who despairs of his Lord's mercy but the astray?' — the same rare verb, the same construction with raḥmah, prohibition and rhetorical question forming one doctrine: qunūṭ is misbelief about Allah.

قنط: 39:53 forbids despairing of Allah's mercy even to those who wronged themselves ↔ 30:36 diagnoses the reflex it forbids — 'when affliction touches them for what their hands sent ahead, at once they despair (yaqnaṭūn)' — diagnosis and prohibition sharing the root.

قنط: 41:49 'if evil touches him he is yaʾūs qanūṭ — despairing, hopeless' ↔ 39:53's address to the very people who have transgressed against themselves: 'do not despair (lā taqnaṭū) of Allah's mercy' — the portrait of the qanūṭ and the door opened out of that state.

أضاء (aḍāʾa): 2:17 the hypocrite's kindled fire 'when it illuminated (aḍāʾat) around him, Allah took away their light' ↔ 2:20 the lightning 'whenever it illuminates (aḍāʾa) for them they walk, when it darkens they stand' — the paired hypocrite parables, each hinged on the same verb of illumination granted then withdrawn.

ضوأ: 2:17 'Allah took away their light and left them in darknesses, unseeing' ↔ 28:71 'if Allah made the night permanent, what god other than Allah could bring you ḍiyāʾ?' — both passages make light a revocable divine grant whose withdrawal leaves absolute darkness, spiritually in al-Baqarah and cosmically in al-Qasas.

رضاعة (raḍāʿah): 2:233 legislates the nursing bond itself — 'mothers shall nurse (yurḍiʿna) their children two complete years... if you wish to have them nursed (tastarḍiʿū)' ↔ 4:23 legislates its legal consequence — 'forbidden to you are the mothers who nursed you (arḍaʿnakum) and your sisters through nursing (mina r-raḍāʿah)' — two halves of one legislative system in which milk creates kinship.

بضاعة (biḍāʿah, merchandise): 12:19 the caravan 'concealed HIM as merchandise (asarrūhu biḍāʿatan)' and sold him cheap ↔ 12:62 Yusuf, now controlling Egypt's stores, orders 'put their biḍāʿah back in their saddlebags' — the boy once traded as goods now refuses to keep his brothers' goods, the surah's economy-of-worth motif inverting.

بضاعة: 12:19 Yusuf hidden as biḍāʿah and sold for counted dirhams ↔ 12:65 the brothers open their baggage and find 'hādhihi biḍāʿatunā ruddat ilaynā' (our merchandise returned to us) — the returned payment reopens the road back to the brother they once sold, the same word carrying the reversal.

بضاعة: 12:19 they sold Yusuf as concealed biḍāʿah for a wretched price ↔ 12:88 the sellers stand before him pleading 'we have come with meager merchandise (biḍāʿatin muzjāh), give us full measure and be charitable' — the surah closes the motif: those who priced him cheap arrive holding worthless goods, dependent on his generosity.

تخطّف (takhaṭṭuf, being snatched away): 29:67 'We made a safe sanctuary while people are snatched away (yutakhaṭṭafu n-nās) all around them' ↔ 8:26 'remember when you were few, fearing that people would snatch you away (yatakhaṭṭafakumu n-nās), and He sheltered you' — the same rare Form-V image of human beings seized by raiders, used to indict Meccan ingratitude for safety and to command Medinan gratitude for it.

مقتصد (muqtaṣid): 35:32 divides the inheritors of the Book — 'among them one who wrongs himself, among them a muqtaṣid, among them a foremost racer' ↔ 5:66 applies the same middle-category label to the People of the Book: 'among them is an ummah muqtaṣidah, but many of them — evil is what they do' — the same rare taxonomic epithet sorting a scripture-bearing community into ranks.

مقتصد: 35:32 'fa-minhum muqtaṣid' as the middle rank of the Book's inheritors ↔ 31:32 'fa-minhum muqtaṣid' — the identical phrase for the sea-rescued who neither fully deny nor fully live their storm-taught sincerity; the Quran reuses one word for the person who stops halfway between wrong and foremost.

سدر (the thorny desert lote tree) as the measure of blessing: 34:16 Saba's two gardens are downgraded to bitter fruit, tamarisk 'and a little sidr' (سِدْرٍ قَلِيلٍ) — the thorny survivor of a punished land — ↔ 56:28 the Companions of the Right dwell in 'sidr makhḍūd' (سِدْرٍ مَّخْضُودٍ), the same tree with its thorns stripped and made abundant: one rare tree deliberately marking blessing withdrawn versus blessing perfected.

دحر: Iblis is sentenced 'ukhruj minhā madh'ūman madḥūran' (7:18 — despised and expelled, double ḥāl) ↔ 17:18 the seeker of the immediate world enters Jahannam 'madhmūman madḥūran' — the follower receives the leader's exact double-ḥāl expulsion sentence, fulfilling 7:18's own oath to fill Jahannam with Iblis and whoever follows him.

دحر: the wisdom-list of al-Isra closes with the mushrik 'cast into Jahannam malūman madḥūran' (17:39), re-applying to humans the madḥūr expulsion pronounced on Iblis in 7:18 — shirk earns the sentence of the one who first refused.

دحر: 7:18 sentences Iblis as madḥūr (expelled), and 37:9 shows the sentence enacted on his kind — the eavesdropping devils are pelted from every side 'duḥūran', driven from the Highest Assembly; the rare root binds the original expulsion decree to its cosmic enforcement.

عقيم: 42:50 gives the root's literal anchor — 'He makes whom He wills barren (ʿaqīman)' as an act of absolute divine sovereignty over generativity — and 22:55 transfers that exact word to time itself, 'the punishment of a barren Day (yawmin ʿaqīm)': the Day that begets no tomorrow, barrenness moved from the womb to history by the same rare adjective.

وقف: 6:27/6:30 'wa law tarā idh wuqifū ʿalā n-nār / ʿalā rabbihim' and 34:31 'wa law tarā idhi ẓ-ẓālimūna mawqūfūna ʿinda rabbihim' share the whole frame — the same 'if you could only see' address opening onto the same scene of the wrongdoers halted before their Lord, the rare judicial-standing root carrying the scene in both.

وقف: the passive standing of 6:27/6:30 ('when they are made to stand before the Fire… before their Lord') appears as the angelic command in 37:24 'wa qifūhum innahum masʾūlūn' — 'halt them: they are to be questioned' — the same arraignment-stop of judgment seen from the other side of the order.

قلم: 96:4 'alladhī ʿallama bil-qalam' — the pen as the instrument by which the Most Generous transmits knowledge to man — ↔ 31:27 every tree on earth as aqlām with seven seas of ink still could not exhaust kalimāt Allah: the same rare noun theologized at both poles, the pen as the medium of divine teaching and the pen as the finite tool that can never contain the divine speech it serves.
