أمد: 72:25 the Prophet is commanded to confess 'I do not know… whether my Lord appoints for it an amad' — the appointed span whose measure is Allah's alone — ↔ 18:12 the sleepers are raised 'to make known which of the two parties best reckoned (aḥṣā) the amad of their stay', a staged contest of counting an amad that the surah then resolves with 'Allah knows best how long they remained': the same rare word for the span whose reckoning defeats human knowledge.

عتب: the closed-door formula 'wa lā hum yustaʿtabūn' — nor will they be invited to make amends — recurs verbatim at the verdict of 45:35 ('this Day they will not be brought out of it, nor asked to make amends') and is given its fullest form in 41:24, which slams both exits at once: 'if they plead to be restored (yastaʿtibū), they are not among the restored (al-muʿtabīn)' — the same rare Form-X judgment formula sealing the end of appeal.

تبر: the cognate-accusative annihilation formula appears only twice in the Quran — 25:39 'wa kullan tabbarnā tatbīran' (each destroyed nation We shattered utterly) and 17:7 'wa liyutabbirū mā ʿalaw tatbīran' (the invaders destroy utterly whatever they overran, as the decreed consequence of Bani Israil's corruption) — the same intensive construction marking total civilizational destruction, once with Allah as direct agent and once through the human instruments He sends.

نكال (nakāl, deterrent-example punishment): 2:66 the Sabbath-breakers made 'a nakāl for what was before it and after it' ↔ 5:38 the thief's hand cut 'nakālan min Allāh' — the same rare technical noun naming punishment whose declared purpose is public deterrence, not mere retribution.

نكال: 2:66 'We made it a nakāl' for onlookers across generations ↔ 79:25 'Allah seized him with the nakāl of the Hereafter and the first life' — Pharaoh, like the Sabbath-breakers, is turned into the standing deterrent-example, and both passages close by naming the audience (mawʿiẓa lil-muttaqīn / ʿibra li-man yakhshā).

نكل: 2:66 nakāl as the punishment-made-example ↔ 4:84 'wa-Llāhu ashaddu tankīlan' — the Form II verbal noun of the same deterrence term, asserting Allah's exemplary punishment outweighs the enemy's might.

شيطان مريد: 22:3 the disputer without knowledge 'follows every shayṭān marīd' ↔ 4:117 those who invoke female idols 'invoke nothing but a shayṭān marīd' — the same rare epithet of the rebel devil applied to the one humans actually end up following/invoking.

شيطان مريد/مارد: 22:3 'every rebellious devil' whom the misguided follow ↔ 37:7 the sky guarded 'from every shayṭān mārid' — the identical rare epithet, the devil rebelling below by misleading and above by storming the Assembly.

قتر (stinginess): 17:100 'if you owned the treasuries of my Lord's mercy you would withhold... wa-kāna l-insānu qatūrā' — man's default grudging nature — ↔ 25:67 the servants of al-Raḥmān 'when they spend are neither wasteful nor stingy (lam yaqturū)': the diagnosed disease and its cured portrait, the root's only two vice-sense uses outside neutral 2:236.

جوع + خوف paired: 16:112 the ungrateful town made to taste 'the garment of hunger and fear (libāsa l-jūʿi wa-l-khawf)' ↔ 2:155 believers tested 'with something of fear and hunger (shay'in mina l-khawfi wa-l-jūʿ)' — the same designed hunger-fear pairing, in full measure as punishment for kufr al-niʿma and in small measure as trial for the patient.

حرص: 16:37 'in taḥriṣ ʿalā hudāhum — if you are eager for their guidance, Allah does not guide whom He lets stray' ↔ 12:103 'wa-mā aktharu l-nāsi wa-law ḥaraṣta bi-mu'minīn — most people, however eager you are, will not believe' — twin addresses to the Prophet bounding his ḥirṣ against the decree.

حرص: 9:128 names 'ḥarīṣun ʿalaykum' as the Messenger's defining trait — the very eagerness for people's faith that 16:37 (in taḥriṣ ʿalā hudāhum) tells him cannot override Allah's withholding of guidance; the trait and its limit share the one rare root.

شرح الصدر inverted: 6:125 'whom Allah wills to guide, He opens his chest to islām (yashraḥ ṣadrahu li-l-islām)' ↔ 16:106 'man sharaḥa bi-l-kufri ṣadrā — whoever opens his chest to kufr' — the same idiom deliberately flipped to mark chosen disbelief against coerced speech.

شرح الصدر: 6:125 the opened chest as the sign of divine guidance ↔ 94:1 'a-lam nashraḥ laka ṣadrak' — the same idiom declared already accomplished in the Prophet, the paradigm case of the chest Allah opens.

فوج: 78:18 'the Day the Trumpet is blown and you come in throngs (afwājā)' ↔ 38:59 'hādhā fawjun muqtaḥimun maʿakum — this is a troop bursting in with you' into the Fire — the same rare troop-word tracks the procession from the muster of the Day of Decision to the gate of Jahannam.

فوج: 78:18 humanity arriving afwājan at the appointed mīqāt ↔ 67:8 'kullamā ulqiya fīhā fawjun — every time a troop is flung into it, its keepers ask: did no warner come to you?' — the throngs of the gathering are processed into the Fire troop by troop.

الأسباط in the fixed prophet-list: 2:136 'what was revealed to Ibrāhīm, Ismāʿīl, Isḥāq, Yaʿqūb and al-asbāṭ' ↔ 4:163 'We revealed to Ibrāhīm, Ismāʿīl, Isḥāq, Yaʿqūb and al-asbāṭ' — the identical rare list-formula, recited as credo in al-Baqarah and restated as the revelation chain that leaves 'no argument against Allah'.

أنقذ from the Fire, mirrored: 3:103 'you were on the brink of a pit of Fire and He rescued you from it (fa-anqadhakum minhā)' ↔ 39:19 'is it you who can rescue (tunqidhu) the one already in the Fire?' — same rare verb, same Fire: Allah's completed rescue versus even the Prophet's impossible one.

نقذ: 36:23 the believer of Ya-Sin rejects gods whose intercession avails nothing 'wa-lā yunqidhūn — nor can they rescue me' ↔ 39:19 not even the Prophet can rescue one on whom the word of punishment came due — rescue-power belongs to Allah alone, denied to idols and intercessors alike by the same verb.

نقذ: 36:43 the drowning 'have no cry answered wa-lā hum yunqadhūn — nor are they rescued — except as mercy from Us' ↔ 39:19 no rescuer from the decreed Fire — both passages use the rare verb to state that rescue is exclusively Allah's act of mercy.

The 'qad khāba man' verdict formula: 91:10 'wa-qad khāba man dassāhā — failed is he who buries it' ↔ 20:61 Musa's warning 'wa-qad khāba mani ftarā — failed is he who fabricates' — the identical rare formula pronouncing definitive failure.

قد خاب من: 91:10 'qad khāba man dassāhā' ↔ 20:111 'wa-qad khāba man ḥamala ẓulmā — failed is he who carries injustice' before al-Ḥayy al-Qayyūm — the same verdict formula, sealing the soul-burier and the ẓulm-carrier alike.

خاب as divine verdict: 91:10's 'qad khāba man dassāhā' ↔ 14:15 'wa-khāba kullu jabbārin ʿanīd — and every obstinate tyrant failed' — the formula's variant closing the contest between messengers and tyrants with the same rare failure-verb.

قوماً بوراً: 25:18 'they forgot the message and became a ruined people (kānū qawman būrā)' ↔ 48:12 'you assumed an evil assumption and became a ruined people (kuntum qawman būrā)' — the only two occurrences of this rare verdict phrase, ruin through forgetting Allah and ruin through thinking ill of Him.

سدّ (barrier): 18:93-94 the vulnerable between 'the two barriers (al-saddayn)' ask Dhul-Qarnayn to build 'saddan' against Yajuj and Majuj ↔ 36:9 'We placed before them a sadd and behind them a sadd... so they do not see' — the same rare noun for a divinely-sanctioned wall, protective around the weak and imprisoning around the deniers; the Ya-Sin tadabbur itself invokes Dhul-Qarnayn's sadd.

زنى: 25:68 ranks zinā in the triad with shirk and murder under doubled punishment (yalqa athāmā) ↔ 24:2 legislates its ḥadd — 'al-zāniyatu wa-l-zānī fa-jlidū' — and forbids pity in enforcing it: the eschatological gravity and the legal penalty of the same named offense.

The same triad restated as pledge: 25:68 'do not invoke another god... do not kill the soul... wa-lā yaznūn' ↔ 60:12 the women's bayʿah 'they will not associate anything with Allah, will not steal, wa-lā yaznīna, will not kill their children' — the servant-portrait's shirk-murder-zinā sequence becomes the covenant text sworn to the Prophet.
خرص formula: 51:10 'qutila l-kharrāṣūn — cursed be the conjecturers' names as a class exactly those of 6:116, the earth's majority who 'follow nothing but assumption, wa-in hum illā yakhruṣūn.'

خرص: 51:10's cursed kharrāṣūn ↔ 6:148 the mushrikūn excusing shirk by decree ('had Allah willed we would not have associated') answered 'in antum illā takhruṣūn — you do nothing but guess' — the same rare verb branding fabricated certainty.
خرص: 51:10 'qutila l-kharrāṣūn' ↔ 10:66 those invoking partners 'follow only conjecture, wa-in hum illā yakhruṣūn' — the recurring closing formula that reduces shirk's epistemology to guessing.

خرص: 51:10's curse on the conjecturers ↔ 43:20 'if al-Raḥmān had willed we would not have worshipped them... in hum illā yakhruṣūn' — the same formula stamped on the same qadar-excuse for idolatry as in 6:148.

الرعب cast into hearts, near-verbatim: 3:151 'sanulqī fī qulūbi lladhīna kafarū l-ruʿb — We will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieve' ↔ 8:12 'sa-ulqī fī qulūbi lladhīna kafarū l-ruʿb' — the identical formula as post-Uhud promise and as Badr enactment revealed to the angels.

الرعب: 3:151's promise 'We will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieve' ↔ 59:2 'wa-qadhafa fī qulūbihim l-ruʿb' — Banū al-Naḍīr, trusting their fortresses, tear down their own houses: the formula fulfilled without a battle.

لزام: 20:129 'were it not for a word that preceded from your Lord and a named term, [the punishment] would have been binding (la-kāna lizāmā)' ↔ 25:77 'you have denied, so it will be binding (fa-sawfa yakūnu lizāmā)' — the word lizām occurs only in these two verses: the deferral of the inevitable and the announcement that the deferral has expired.

دأب: 8:52/8:54 'ka-daʾbi āli firʿawna wa-lladhīna min qablihim' — the fixed formula for the habit of the deniers — ↔ 40:31 where the believer inside Pharaoh's own court warns 'mithla daʾbi qawmi Nūḥin wa-ʿĀdin wa-Thamūd': the same rare 'habit' formula, turned back on āl Firʿawn by one of their own.

zūr (speech bent away from reality): 22:30 commands 'wa-jtanibū qawla z-zūr' in the same breath as shunning idols ↔ 25:4 the disbelievers brand the Quran itself 'ifkun iftarāhu... zūran' — the very category Allah forbids is the word they hurl at revelation.

22:30 'shun qawl az-zūr' ↔ 58:2 zihar declared 'munkaran mina l-qawli wa-zūran' — the same term for reality-twisting speech, here applied by Allah to the utterance that tried to remake a wife into a mother.

ḍayf of the one angelic visitation: 51:24 'ḍayfi Ibrāhīma l-mukramīn' honored at Ibrahim's table ↔ 11:78 the same messengers arrive as Lut's ḍayf and the mob rushes his house — two stations of a single narrative told across surahs.

51:24 the honored guests of Ibrahim ↔ 15:68 Lut pleads 'inna hāʾulāʾi ḍayfī fa-lā tafḍaḥūn' — the same guests in the next station of the story, the word ḍayf carrying the hospitality-sanctity the city violates.

The rain→crops sign-list repeats item for item: 80:27-29 'fa-anbatnā fīhā ḥabban... wa-zaytūnan wa-nakhlan' ↔ 16:11 'yunbitu lakum bihi z-zarʿa wa-z-zaytūna wa-n-nakhīla wa-l-aʿnāb', both closing on a call to reflect — the olive is a fixed member of the Quran's recurring provision argument.

andād: 2:22 'fa-lā tajʿalū lillāhi andādan wa-antum taʿlamūn' — the Quran's opening prohibition — returns in 2:165 as diagnosis: 'man yattakhidhu min dūni llāhi andādan yuḥibbūnahum ka-ḥubbi llāh' — the rival-equals are not merely posited but loved.

2:22 forbids setting up andād to the Creator ↔ 14:30 'wa-jaʿalū lillāhi andādan li-yuḍillū ʿan sabīlih' — the identical construction, now the settled practice of those who exchanged Allah's blessing for kufr.

2:22 'do not make andād for Allah' ↔ 34:33 the weakened testify against their leaders on the Day: 'idh taʾmurūnanā an nakfura billāhi wa-najʿala lahū andādan' — the forbidden act of 2:22 replayed as courtroom accusation.

2:22's prohibition of andād ↔ 39:8 the man who cried to his Lord in harm then, once relieved, 'jaʿala lillāhi andādan li-yuḍilla ʿan sabīlih' — comfort re-manufactures the exact rivals the first command outlawed.

faziʿa of the Day: 27:87 'yawma yunfakhu fī ṣ-ṣūri fa-faziʿa man fī s-samāwāti wa-man fī l-arḍ' ↔ 34:51 'wa-law tarā idh faziʿū fa-lā fawt' — the same verb for the universal terror at the summons, once at the trumpet, once at the seizure from a near place with no escape.

ḥaṣīd for annihilated communities: 11:100 the towns 'minhā qāʾimun wa-ḥaṣīd' — some standing, some mown down — ↔ 10:24 the earth at peak adornment 'jaʿalnāhā ḥaṣīdan ka-an lam taghna bi-l-ams': the same mown-field image for a flourishing world cut in one stroke.
11:100's towns as ḥaṣīd ↔ 21:15 'ḥattā jaʿalnāhum ḥaṣīdan khāmidīn' — here the wrongdoing populations themselves become the harvested stubble; judgment as reaping is the identical metaphor.

The dunya-rain parable shares a verbatim clause: 10:24 and 18:45 both read 'ka-māʾin anzalnāhu mina s-samāʾi fa-khtalaṭa bihī nabātu l-arḍ' — the same parable told twice, once ending as ḥaṣīd overnight, once as chaff scattered by the winds.

The ʿalaqah stage of the creation sequence: 23:14 'khalaqnā n-nuṭfata ʿalaqatan' ↔ 75:38 'thumma kāna ʿalaqatan fa-khalaqa fa-sawwā' — the same nuṭfah→ʿalaqah chain deployed as the argument for resurrection.
23:14's ʿalaqah stage ↔ 96:2 'khalaqa l-insāna min ʿalaq' — the first revealed ayahs name man's origin by the same clinging-clot term the creation-stages passages elaborate step by step.

The damned wish for one more turn: 39:58 'law anna lī karratan fa-akūna mina l-muḥsinīn' ↔ 26:102 'fa-law anna lanā karratan fa-nakūna mina l-muʾminīn' — a near-verbatim formula, singular and plural voices of the same impossible plea.
39:58's longed-for karrah ↔ 79:12 the deniers scoff 'tilka idhan karratun khāsirah' — the same rare noun for the return-to-life, mocked before death and begged for after it.

The Quran as shifāʾ: 17:82 'nunazzilu mina l-qurʾāni mā huwa shifāʾun wa-raḥmatun lil-muʾminīn' ↔ 10:57 'shifāʾun li-mā fī ṣ-ṣudūr' — the same claim that revelation itself heals the unseen disease of the breast, with 41:44 completing the triad.

sakrah as blinding stupor without wine: 50:19 'wa-jāʾat sakratu l-mawti bi-l-ḥaqq' ↔ 15:72 'la-fī sakratihim yaʿmahūn' — Lut's people blundering in desire-drunkenness meet, in Qaf, the death-stupor that ends every intoxication with the truth one had dodged.

50:19's sakrat al-mawt ↔ 22:2 'wa-tarā n-nāsa sukārā wa-mā hum bi-sukārā' — people staggering as if wine-drunk at the Hour; both passages use intoxication for consciousness overwhelmed when unveiled reality arrives.

ḥuṭām as the crop's end-state in the dunya argument: 57:20 the rain-parable closes 'thumma yakūnu ḥuṭāman' ↔ 56:65 'law nashāʾu la-jaʿalnāhu ḥuṭāman' — the harvest you did not create can be crushed to the same debris; 39:21 (already linked to both) completes the triple.

nakth of sworn bonds: 48:10 'fa-man nakatha fa-innamā yankuthu ʿalā nafsih' ↔ 9:12 'wa-in nakathū aymānahum min baʿdi ʿahdihim... fa-qātilū aʾimmata l-kufr' — the same verb for snapping a formal oath, stated as universal principle in al-Fath and as case law for the treaty-breakers in Tawbah.
48:10's pledge-breaker who only breaks against himself ↔ 9:13 'qawman nakathū aymānahum wa-hammū bi-ikhrāji r-rasūl' — nakth as the identifying mark of those whose oaths carry no binding reality.

afāʾa as the technical term for fayʾ war-gains: 59:7 'mā afāʾa llāhu ʿalā rasūlihi min ahli l-qurā' with its distribution rule ↔ 33:50 'mimmā afāʾa llāhu ʿalayk' defining what is lawful to the Prophet from that same category — the identical legal verb for wealth Allah 'returned' without battle.

qāriʿah appears in the Quran only here, 69:4, and 13:31: 101:1-3 hammers the Day's name al-Qāriʿah three times, 69:4 says Thamūd and ʿĀd denied al-qāriʿah, and 13:31 turns the same rare striking-noun onto the present — 'a qāriʿah keeps striking the disbelievers for what they made, or lands near their home, until Allah's promise comes' — worldly strikes bearing the very name of the Day being denied.

ʿuṣbah: 12:8 — the brothers license their plot against innocent Yusuf with 'wa-naḥnu ʿuṣbah' (we are a strong band); 24:11 names the slander-ring against Aisha 'ʿuṣbatun minkum' (a band from among you). In both, a self-assured inner band wrongs an innocent with a fabricated story, and both wounds are divinely reframed as good (12:100's subtle mercy; 24:11 'do not reckon it evil — it is good for you') — a parallel the ifk narrative consciously inherits from the Yusuf story.

kaẓm: Ya'qub is 'kaẓīm' — grief choked back and poured out only to Allah (12:84-86) — the lived embodiment of 3:134's 'al-kāẓimīna al-ghayẓ', where holding in what the chest carries is legislated as a mark of the people of the Garden.

Identical epithet kaẓīm: Ya'qub choked with grief over a lost son (12:84) versus the jāhilī father whose face darkens 'wa-huwa kaẓīm' at news of a daughter (16:58) — the same word contrasting grief mastered in faith with grief curdling into resentment at Allah's allotment of children.

Same participle, same choked-throat image: Ya'qub 'kaẓīm' holds grief in his chest in the dunyā; 40:18 shows the wrongdoers on the Day 'hearts at the throats, kāẓimīn' — the root's single image of emotion jammed in the throat, once as patience and once as terror.

43:17 repeats 16:58's clause verbatim — 'ẓalla wajhuhu muswaddan wa-huwa kaẓīm' — the father choked at daughter-news; against him stands Ya'qub (12:84), the father whose kaẓm over a child turns to hope and complaint to Allah, not shame.

The two grief-choked prophets: Ya'qub 'fa-huwa kaẓīm' (12:84) complains only to Allah and waits, while 68:48 warns 'be not like the companion of the fish who cried out wa-huwa makẓūm' — the same root dividing the kaẓm that waits for the decree from the kaẓm that cried out before it.

arda/tardā: 20:16 warns Musa 'let not one who disbelieves in it and follows his desire bar you from it fa-tardā (lest you perish)'; 37:56 stages exactly that peril survived — 'ta-llāhi in kidta la-turdīn' (by Allah, you nearly ruined me), said from Paradise to the denying companion who almost did the barring.

Causative ardā naming the agent of one's perdition in judgment-scene speech: 37:56 'in kidta la-turdīn' — the qarīn almost ruined me — and 41:23 'that assumption of yours about your Lord ardākum (ruined you)': the misleading companion and the false ẓann as the named ruiners.

6:137: the shirk-partners beautified the killing of children 'li-yurdūhum' — to bring them to ruin; 37:56 shows the same causative verb from the other side of the grave — the companion who 'almost ruined me' — misleaders as the agents of ardā in both.

iṣrār: 3:135's forgiven are those who 'do not persist (lam yuṣirrū) in what they did while they know'; 45:8's condemned man 'hears the verses of Allah recited, then persists (yuṣirru), arrogant, as if he never heard them' — the same verb splitting the two destinies at the same hinge of knowing.

56:46 indicts the Companions of the Left with the same verb: 'they used to persist (yuṣirrūna) in the great violation' — iṣrār as the damning charge whose refusal (3:135 'wa-lam yuṣirrū') defines the people of the Garden.

71:7: Nuh's people 'aṣarrū wa-stakbarū istikbāran' — persistence welded to arrogance exactly as in 45:8's 'yuṣirru mustakbiran' — while 3:135 names the counter-people whose mark is refusing that persistence.

ḥabl in Aal-Imran: 3:103 commands the community 'hold fast to the ḥabl of Allah, all together, and do not fragment'; nine ayahs later 3:112 shows the alternative — humiliation strikes 'illā bi-ḥablin min Allāh wa-ḥablin min al-nās' — the same rope-image naming both what binds the ummah from within and the only cords that shelter those who let it go.

maghram: 52:40 and 68:46 ask verbatim 'am tas'aluhum ajran fa-hum min maghramin muthqalūn' — is a demanded wage the burden that repels them? — and 9:98 shows that very psychology in the flesh: the bedouin 'takes what he spends as a maghram', the same rare noun for religion misperceived as crushing financial loss.

lawḥ as the medium of divine writing: 7:145 'We wrote for him upon the alwāḥ… admonition and detail of everything' — the Torah on tablets Musa can carry, throw down, and retake — versus 85:22 the Quran 'fī lawḥin maḥfūẓ': the same writing-surface word, but guarded where no hand or fire reaches; the earthly tablets can be shattered, the preserved Tablet cannot.

Verbatim formula 'aynamā thuqifū': 3:112 'humiliation is struck upon them wherever they are found' and 33:61 'accursed — wherever they are found, they are seized and utterly slain' — the same rare passive verb inside the same conditional frame, pronouncing a standing sentence; the ḥaythu-thaqiftumūhum combat twins (2:191, 4:91) already link to this node.

The Quran's only two 'wa-alḥiqnī bi-ṣ-ṣāliḥīn' duas: Ibrahim at the opening of his mission (26:83) and Yusuf at the summit of worldly power and reunion (12:101) — both prophets asking not for rank but to be attached to the righteous cohort, the second echoing the first word for word.

The dua answered in kind: what Ibrahim (26:83) and Yusuf (12:101) beg with 'alḥiqnī bi-ṣ-ṣāliḥīn', Allah performs with the same causative verb in 52:21 — 'alḥaqnā bihim dhurriyyatahum' — joining the offspring of believers to them in the Garden without diminishing their deeds.

multaḥad occurs exactly twice in the Quran: 18:27 tells the Prophet 'recite what has been revealed… wa-lan tajida min dūnihi multaḥadan' and 72:22 puts the same clause in his own mouth — 'lan ajida min dūnihi multaḥadan' — command and confession of the no-refuge-but-Him formula, near-verbatim across surahs.

dhara'a fī al-arḍ: 67:24 and 23:79 are the twin 'He scattered you in the earth and to Him you will be gathered'; 16:13 runs the same rare sowing-verb the other way — 'and what He scattered for you in the earth, diverse in its colors' — creation strewn across the earth as a sign for mankind, mankind strewn across it for the gathering.

furush of the Garden — the noun's only two paradise uses: 55:54 'reclining upon furush whose linings are of istabraq' and 56:34 'wa-furushin marfūʿah' — consecutive surahs seating the rewarded on raised, richly-lined couches inside the same garden-tableau genre.

uḥṣira — the passive occurs exactly twice in the Quran, both in al-Baqarah: 2:196 'fa-in uḥṣirtum' (the pilgrim blocked from completing the rites is granted the easy hady) and 2:273 'alladhīna uḥṣirū fī sabīli-llāh' (the poor pinned down in Allah's cause, unable to travel and earn, are assigned the community's charity) — the same rare form naming the believer immobilized on Allah's path, each time answered with divine accommodation.

The same demolition of Makkan confidence from two directions: 68:37 'am lakum kitābun fīhi tadrusūn' (or do you have a book in which you study, granting you whatever you choose?) and 34:44 'wa-mā ātaynāhum min kutubin yadrusūnahā' (We gave them no books to study, nor sent them a warner before you) — darasa marking the studied scriptural warrant the confident deniers demonstrably lack.
